rodrigo dorez.name: Rodrigo Dorez
rodrigo dorez.origin: Rodrigo Dorez's plantation and ranch is attacked by a myriad of ants that destroy all the crops and livestock. To combat the ants, Rodrigo uses any means, including the use of insecticide but without obtaining any results. He then decides to save the plantation by creating a moat and filling it with flammable liquid to create a barrier of fire. He put his natives to work, but the ants were reaching the plantation without the ditch being completed, so to delay them he decided to sacrifice his native workers, and while the ants devoured the workers, Rodrigo finished the ditch and set it on fire, but the mass of ant corpses put out the fire in one point and from there the ants poured over the moat, reached Rodrigo and devoured him.

However, Peter Parker, posing as an intern to run into Dr. Connors, randomly selected Guevara's badge and bid the oblivious receptionist "Gracias". Soon after, the real Rodrigo was thrown out by Oscorp security guards. It is unknown what happened to Guevara afterwards.

roger.name: Roger
roger.origin: When the Net Prophet frequented the Cyberspace bar the 'Holy Row', he met a woman named Sintilla. Her abusive boyfriend Roger attacked John. John shrugged off his cyberspace attacks and then 'trapped' the man in a loop, making him think his limbs had been severed in real life. Sintilla kissed him and memories began flooding in. He then mysteriously vanished.

roger red right hand.name: Roger (Red Right Hand)
roger red right hand.origin: ===Origin=== When Roger was driving his wife, Carol, to the hospital to give birth to their first born, they got caught on Highway 18 during a fight between Wolverine and The Hulk. Their car was destroyed by Wolverine while he was trying to stop a rampaging Hulk. Roger then tried to carry his wife to the hospital but she and the baby died on the way. He always blamed Wolverine, even though the news said he saved the day. For the next year or so he would stand outside of the X-Men mansion cursing Wolverine's name then he would get drunk. On occasion, he would find a bum, force him to dress-up in a Wolverine costume, and beat him with a bat, killing him. ===Making a Deal with the Devil=== Then one night he was approached by an old man in a bar who told him he could help him, but Roger didn't care and decided to dress another homeless man as Wolverine and beat him to death, but soon after he was approached by a demon who explained that if Roger would join the old man's organization The Red Right Hand, the demon would help him get his revenge. Roger agreed and went back to the bar where he met the old man and told him he wanted to join his organization and he knew how to make Wolverine suffer. Now part of the Red Right Hand, Roger was now known as "The Husband", shortly after the Husband and the Red Right Hand sacrificed a man and of woman in order to invoke the demon, the demon then told them what they should do next. This is how the Red Right Hand made the deal with the devil to possess Wolverine's body, and send his soul to Hell. When The Founder created this criminal organization, Daken discovered its existence and joined them in order to help them get their revenge against Wolverine. To that end, Daken decided to find his father’s children all around the world through the years, he then gave them to the Red Right Hand and on his advice, the criminal organization trained them in order to use them as weapons against Logan. Daken knew that they wouldn't stand a chance against Logan but having his father killing them would hurt him in the worst way possible. Those children would be known as the Mongrels. But the Husband didn't care about Daken's plan and only wanted to send Wolverine's soul to hell, but the other members of the criminal organization decided otherwise. After sending Wolverine's soul to Hell and using the Mongrels to hurt his loved ones, Wolverine escaped from Hell and invaded the Red Right Hand's base in Mexico where he was confronted by the Mongrels. ===Death=== As the members of the Red Right Hand were watching Wolverine fighting the Mongrels, the Husband started to lose his patience and his temper, thinking that it wasn't enough, Wolverine had to know what he did to him. As a result, he became violent and threatened The Founder with his bat as he wanted to leave and attack Wolverine on his own, but before he could Gunhawk killed him under orders of The Founder.

roger aubrey.name: Roger Aubrey
roger aubrey.origin: thumb|left|Roger Aubrey as Dyna-Mite ===Origin=== Accompanying his friend Brian Falsworth to Nazi Germany just prior to the outbreak of World War II, Roger Aubrey became a captive of the Reich upon war breaking out. He was subjected to experiments conducted by Colonel Dietrich, and was shrunk to a height of 12 inches. Brainwashed, he returned to the U.K. as Dyna-Mite to become a member of the Crusaders, a group of Allied superheroes who each unwittingly owed their powers to the Nazis. Unknown to the team, their ally Alfie was a German agent, and the group had been formed with the intention of discrediting the Invaders and assassinating King George VI. After encountering the Invaders, Alfie's villainy was exposed by Roger and the evil plan was thwarted. Colonel Dietrich was subsequently captured and forced to reverse the process which shrank Roger; Aubrey then took on the new identity of the Destroyer (recently abandoned by Brian Falsworth), and went behind enemy lines to continue the fight. ===Modern Times=== Once the war ended, Roger joined Brian and several other heroes in secretly forming a covert group, the V-Battalion, dedicated to preventing anyone like Hitler from ever again threatening the peace of the world. When Brian died in a car crash in 1953, Roger offered to take on the identity as a tribute to his lover, but was denied by Brian's father Montgomery. Instead he soldiered on as the Destroyer, leading the V-Battalion into the 21st century. He was forced to re-evaluate his aggressive position after being temporarily killed, and handed over the Battalion's leadership to the more moral hands of Jim Hammond (the Human Torch). When the Thin Man revived the Invaders, Roger became wary of his true goals and began to investigate. He called on the group for assistance against the forces of Baroness Blood, during which fight he came to accept Joseph Chapman as a worthy Union Jack successor to Brian. Following this, Roger and his ally Hammond confronted the Thin Man and effectively deposed him as leader of the Invaders. ===The Century Game=== Roger later joined Radio Company, a ham radio club, alongside Steve Rogers, Pam, a Korean War nurse, and John Koroki, a former rocket scientist. During one of their meetings, the group heard a coded message being broadcast from an unknown source. With Roger's help, the message was decoded and revealed the location of a potential terrorist attack, which was subsequently thwarted by Steve and the Winter Soldier. Radio Company continued to monitor the broadcasts and decode the messages; Roger theorizing they were part of a game-like global conspiracy to influence world events. The last message lead Captain America to a power plant in Germany called The Forge where he uncovered the Outer Circle, a shadowy organization that had a hand in many key moments throughout the 20th and 21st centuries. Roger used his contacts and discovered that the Outer Circle, via A.I.M., was planning something and offered his assistance to Steve. Roger met with Steve, Sharon and Peggy Carter, Nick Fury, Black Widow, Hawkeye, and Outer Circle defector The Redacted, and concluded that A.I.M. were after an underground facility in lower Manhattan once belonging to Arnim Zola. The group planned to meet in two days to stake out the location but were ambushed by the Outer Circle's agent: M.O.D.O.C., the Mental Organism Designed Only for Control, an alternate form of M.O.D.O.K., who erased their memories and scattered them around the country. The group was missing five days and in that time, A.I.M. took over Lower Manhattan. Regaining their memories with the help of Emma Frost, the heroes regrouped as a new iteration of the Invaders and prepared to liberate Manhattan. The Invaders split up into three sub-teams, each with a specific task. Roger and Sharon were tasked with destroying A.I.M.'s command center. During their mission, the two quickly became friends, with Roger telling Sharon about his past adventures and his relationship with Brian. After destroying the command center, Roger, along with the rest of the Invaders, was again confronted by M.O.D.O.C., who placed them all in their own mind prison where they were forced to relive painful memories. Roger managed to free himself and the rest of the team, and subdue M.O.D.O.C.. However, M.O.D.O.C. reverted to M.O.D.O.K. and shot Roger with a blast of energy, killing him instantly. ===Legacy=== Roger was laid to rest in his native England next to Brian following a memorial service attended by his friends and former teammates from the Invaders, V-Battalion, and Crusaders. In Roger's honor, Sharon took up the mantle of the Destroyer and vowed to continue his fight against evil.

roger bochs.name: Roger Bochs
roger bochs.origin: Roger Bochs was unable to walk, having had both his legs amputated below the knee. While trying do deal with his resulting psychological issues, he was checked into a clinic. Once there, he quickly befriended another patient, Madison Jeffries. Bochs was a genius inventor and developed a robot he nicknamed Box (a play on his own last name) that could act for him. He joined the Canadian government organization, Department H, as part of their superhero program. James MacDonald Hudson, H's top agent and founder, worked on similar cybernetic technology for his power suit, and helped Roger develop the tele-presence tech necessary to project his consciousness into Box. Bochs was a part of Alpha Flight's training group Beta Flight at the time Department H was shut down by the government. Bochs was then recruited by the android Delphine Courtney to be part of the villainous team Omega Flight, who were organized by Jerome Jaxon to defeat Alpha Flight and James Hudson. However, Bochs remained loyal to Hudson and joined Omega Flight merely to infiltrate it. Jerome Jaxon was suspicious and stole Boch's control helmet. Jaxon fought Guardian using the Box robot, but was killed by feedback. Still angry at Jaxon, and wanting to help Alpha Flight, what with Guardian being feared lost, Bochs had Madison Jeffries assist him on a new Box model that the operator would 'phase' into rather than using a control helmet. Bochs encountered Alpha Flight for the first time during the death of Walter Langkowski and his Sasquatch body. Bochs allowed Shaman to place Langkowski's spirit into the robot temporarily. When Langkowski's spirit was lost at the Crossroads of all Realities, Bochs became Box again and started working with Alpha Flight as a full-time member. Later, Bochs was briefly confined to the robot after suffering from 'the bends' in a deep sea mission when he phased out of the armor at crushing depths. Bochs sought help from Madison's brother; Lionel was gifted with the mutant ability to affect organic material in the same way as Madison could metal. Lionel gave Bochs a younger body and restored his legs in order for Bochs to appear more attractive to his flirtatious teammate Aurora. However, the insane Lionel used decaying organic material to do so, and it soon decomposed. Bochs became insanely jealous of Aurora's "wandering eye" and attacked her. Madison was able to stop Bochs by trapping him in the Box robot. Alpha Flight took Bochs to Lionel to see if he could cure Bochs of his seeming insanity. Scramble and Bochs merged themselves into a being called Omega, which they were able to create with their combined intellect and power. Bochs apparently awoke from his psychosis when Madison Jeffries confronted the two using Box. Persuasion was able to separate the two. However, Scramble lobotomized Bochs in order to remain as Omega. Omega was destroyed by Box (Madison Jeffries) who took over the Box robot, killing both Bochs and Lionel.

Bochs was then recruited by the android Delphine Courtney to be part of the villainous team Omega Flight, who were organized by Jerome Jaxon to defeat Alpha Flight and James Hudson. However, Bochs remained loyal to Hudson and joined Omega Flight merely to infiltrate it. Jerome Jaxon was suspicious and stole Boch's control helmet. Jaxon fought Guardian using the Box robot, but was killed by feedback. Still angry at Jaxon, and wanting to help Alpha Flight, what with Guardian being feared lost, Bochs had Madison Jeffries assist him on a new Box model that the operator would 'phase' into rather than using a control helmet. Bochs encountered Alpha Flight for the first time during the death of Walter Langkowski and his Sasquatch body. Bochs allowed Shaman to place Langkowski's spirit into the robot temporarily. When Langkowski's spirit was lost at the Crossroads of all Realities, Bochs became Box again and started working with Alpha Flight as a full-time member. Later, Bochs was briefly confined to the robot after suffering from 'the bends' in a deep sea mission when he phased out of the armor at crushing depths. Bochs sought help from Madison's brother; Lionel was gifted with the mutant ability to affect organic material in the same way as Madison could metal. Lionel gave Bochs a younger body and restored his legs in order for Bochs to appear more attractive to his flirtatious teammate Aurora. However, the insane Lionel used decaying organic material to do so, and it soon decomposed. Bochs became insanely jealous of Aurora's "wandering eye" and attacked her. Madison was able to stop Bochs by trapping him in the Box robot. Alpha Flight took Bochs to Lionel to see if he could cure Bochs of his seeming insanity. Scramble and Bochs merged themselves into a being called Omega, which they were able to create with their combined intellect and power. Bochs apparently awoke from his psychosis when Madison Jeffries confronted the two using Box. Persuasion was able to separate the two. However, Scramble lobotomized Bochs in order to remain as Omega. Omega was destroyed by Box (Madison Jeffries) who took over the Box robot, killing both Bochs and Lionel.

roger bochs jr.name: Roger Bochs Jr.
roger bochs jr.origin: Son of the famous Roger Bochs, scientist and engineer, Roger Jr. suffered from the same congenital condition that robbed his father of his legs at birth. thumb|left|Bochs wearing his armor As a student at the Braddock Academy, Roger operated in an exoskeleton-style construct based on his father's original design but modified to increase his speed and strength ten-fold. He attended a meeting of which includes other schools for a Contest of Champions between the students from every Institute. However, the Contest was interrupted when Thanos' forces descended upon Earth. After graduating, Roger followed his father's footsteps in becoming a pioneer in biotech engineering and became known for his groundbreaking in the field of robotics for people with disabilities. Roger was recruited by Department H to oversee the development of Box Sentinels to supplement Alpha Flight in capturing mutant fugitives in Canada. When Feedback was spotted in Bend, Oregon, Director Erika Doiron deployed Box Sentinels to capture him while Roger controlled them remotely from Department H Headquarters. Roger lost his composure when Feedback destroyed several units but calmed down when a Sentinel immobilized him. When Feedback argued he did nothing wrong, Roger retorted through one of his Sentinels that he was already breaking the law for being a mutant. Roger was shocked by Alpha Flight's mutant splinter group who arrived to rescue Feedback. Due to the constant bickering between Roger and Doiron, several Sentinels were damaged and destroyed during the battle by the splinter group, who were able to teleport away with Feedback although Roger was able to pinpoint their location in Turtle Mountain, Manitoba. Roger later surveyed the damage done to the Sentinels and made notes on how to improve them. While Alpha Flight escorted Feedback back to headquarters on their Omnijet, Department H detected mutant presence at Krakoa North nearby and Roger directed the Sentinels accompanying the Omnijet there. As the Sentinels were rounding up the Krakoa North inhabitants, Argent destroyed a Sentinel, to which Roger instinctively had another Sentinel attack him. To Roger's horror, an energy blast from the Sentinel killed Argent. A shocked Roger silently fixated on the image of Argent's smoldering corpse as the Alpha Flight splinter group returned to rescue the mutants. Doiron continued to berate Roger by convincing him Argent's death was justified and threatened to replace him if he didn't obey commands. Roger regained his senses but Nemesis had already teleported her mutant teammates and the refugees away. Roger had the Sentinels detain the remaining Alpha Flight members, who were revealed to have been helping the mutants the entire time. After the battle, Roger continued to express remorse for Argent's death.

roger brokeridge.name: Roger Brokeridge
roger brokeridge.species: Human, mutated by the Power Broker process
roger brokeridge.first_appearance: Civil War: Battle Damage Report Vol 1 1
roger brokeridge.origin: ===Origin=== Roger Brokeridge was born in a middle class suburb of Los Angeles, his early life is mostly unknown. At some point his brother Paul got enhancements from a new Power Broker, giving him an immense physique and strength. Paul then joined the Unlimited Class Wrestling Federation, but suffered an intense injury, leaving him immobile, and costing his parents an immense amount to treat him. Angry over how this was affecting his family, Roger tried to work up the courage to kill his brother and end their familial suffering, but he ultimately couldn't do it. Deciding, instead, to kill the Power Broker for giving his brother the powers, Roger approached him, but was ultimately convinced to gain power himself. Undergoing an immensely painful procedure, he gained the ability to create balls of hard light. Intending to turn to crime in order to help pay off his debts to the Power Broker, Roger cased the route of an armored truck. When he finally planned to rob the truck, he accidentally prevented the truck from hitting a young girl. Thinking he had saved the girl on purpose, the guards thanked him. An arriving Wonder Man also thanked him, and convinced him to the join the Initiative. Since becoming a hero wasn't profitable, the Power Broker sold his contract to Hydra. ===Initiative=== thumb|left|Roger Brokeridge One of the new Initiative recruits that arrived with Rage, Cloud 9, MVP, and others, Brokeridge displayed an outgoing and arrogant personality, hitting on Thor Girl on the bus ride in and cracking a joke about not having a cape when receiving his fatigues. During the training mishap with Armory he exhibited the ability to create an energy ball that deflected the lethal blasts from Armory's Tactigon. On his first mission, he helped defend the President against an assault from Hydra. As he returned from the mission, he accidentally witnessed Komodo depowered while she slept. Awaking, Komodo grew angry and attacked him, only backing off when forced to by Gauntlet. Arriving back at Camp Hammond, he was involved in a several training exercises, including being taught water safety by Stingray. At the end of the day, he participated in an assault exercise with several of his teammates as they attempted to "assault" the Thing. After this final exercise, he headed into town where he was treated as a villain until Senator Arthur Woodman, a Hydra agent approached him with knowledge of Roger's real name. Woodman then forced Roger to steal a vial of Super-Power Inhibiting Nanobots from Camp Hammond, causing problems later on for Iron Man when he battled the Hulk during World War Hulk. Brokeridge was present at Camp Hammond when KIA, a rogue clone of the deceased MVP, attacked the trainees and their mentors, in a hunt for anyone present when MVP was killed as well as those involved in the ensuing coverup. Brokeridge and Komodo were caught fraternising moments before the attack began. Brokeridge accompanied Komodo and Cloud 9 to Tennessee through a Negative Zone portal in an attempt to use another clone to help shut down KIA but the group were attacked by a recently reformed New Warriors who would call themselves Counter Force, who believed they might be being misled by the Initiative. When KIA arrived and attacked, Brokeridge helped to fight against him alongside the others, and had to amputate Komodo's damaged legs so she could regrow them. Soon after this he attended the funeral of Trauma, who returned to life during the viewing of his body. Roger along with Komodo, Cloud 9, Ultra Girl, 3-D Man, Thor Girl, and Trauma. All of which, with the exception of Trauma, were given states to protect as graduated members of The Initiative, along with new costumes. Roger was then assigned to Nevada's Initiative team, the Heavy Hitters. During the Skrull invasion Roger and the Heavy Hitters, including Gravity, Nonstop, and Telemetry, helped the Skrull Kill Krew and 3-D Man deal with a Skrull infiltrator posing as an unnamed Heavy Hitters team member. He then left with Komodo, 3-D Man, and the Krew to help the other Initiative teams. ===Dark Reign=== After the invasion, Hardball's status as an agent for Hydra led to a confrontation against the rest of the Heavy Hitters and a visiting Komodo. Hardball killed Senator Woodman, effectively becoming the new leader of Woodman's Hydra cell. This ended his relationship to the Initiative and to a saddened Komodo as well. Hardball was revealed to be running a Hydra training camp in Madripoor and became the lover of Scorpion (Carmilla Black). The Shadow Initiative arrived in Madripoor to capture him, only to be caught off guard with enhanced S.P.I.N. Tech darts that blocked Komodo's powers. The Shadow Initiative briefly retreats, returning and claiming they wish to switch sides, allowing them to gain access to the Hydra base's weapons, and take them down from within. During the fight, it was revealed that Hardball only joined Hydra because he had no alternative. He willingly surrender

roger browning.name: Roger Browning
roger browning.origin: Roger Browning was an agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. before the organization collapsed. Browning then took up selling whatever S.H.I.E.L.D. intelligence he was able to get his hands on to the higher bidder, including information regarding a powerful Level 10 asset known as the Obelisk. Director Phil Coulson of the newly reformed S.H.I.E.L.D. hired a team of mercenaries - including Izzy Hartley, Lance Hunter, and Idaho - to buy the information from Browning. As they were making out the details of their transaction, a superpowered Hydra assassin named Carl Creel took them all by surprise, and killed Browning.

roger dicken.name: Roger Dicken
roger dicken.origin: The man who would become Captain Wings possibly came from an upper middle class English background. He, like his fellow Crusaders, was a great patriot of his country and had wanted to help by enlisting for military service. Unfortunately they were all rejected for various reasons; Captain Wings had a slight heart murmur, which kept him from joining the RAF. The Nazi secret agent code-named Alfie used this sense of duty to recruit all the members of the Crusaders, which was really a plan to assassinate the king of England and discredit the Invaders. After being given his special wings, Captain Wings joined the newly formed super-hero team called the Crusaders. The next part of Alfie's scheme was to have the team gain credibility by assisting the Home Guard with the aftermath of a planned German bombing raid. Since Captain Wings, Thunderfist, and Tommy Lightning were in the area of the attack, they were able to beat the Invaders to the location of a fire and help stop it from rapidly blazing out of control. Captain Wings personally swooped into a burning building and flew two people to safety, while his teammates dealt with other emergency situations. Afterwards, the Invaders arrived and the two teams greeted each other, however when Captain America enquired about the source of their powers the Crusaders mysteriously departed with haste. That same day the Crusader named Dyna-Mite saved the life of King George VI from an assassin, while the Invaders where led off on a diversion set by Alfie. For their quick assistance and the notable late arrival of the Invaders yet again, the Crusaders were named his majesty's new personal honor guard. Later that night, on board a boat moored at a darkened dock on the Thames river, the members of the Crusaders were each expressing a feeling that something was wrong and an unease with them guarding the king. A major concern among them all was a lack of knowledge of how their powers truly worked and just why they had been chosen to wield them. Suddenly Alfie arrived and the team preceded to question him about these matters, and so he showed them a belt, that he wore, which controlled the source of their powers; he then demonstrated that he could to turn them off as easily as a radio. He further explained that it had been their sense of patriotism that had led to their being chosen, and with their new powers they were now more valuable than an entire regiment when it came to protecting his Majesty. When the idea that the Invaders could just as easily guard the king if they were not able to, Alfie called the Invaders Nazi agents and produced a bunch of photographs to backup his claim. In fact, he even stated that this had been the reason that the Crusaders had been created and in the end he managed to convince most of the team that he was a liaison for the British Royal Navy. The next day, while the Crusaders were guarding King George VI at a christening ceremony for a new naval vessel, Captain Wings was pondering the absence of Dyna-Mite. When the Invaders suddenly arrived and tried to stop the king from smashing the bottle against the hull of the ship. The Crusaders leapt into action to protect his Majesty from what they thought were Nazi agents, with Ghost Girl and Captain Wings both confronting Toro. The king decided to finish the ceremony and then go to safety, but the Human Torch snatched the bottle and threw it to the Sub-Mariner, who hurled it out to sea where it exploded. This brought a realization that it had been a boobytrap set by Alfie, who was killed soon afterwards when his car fell off a bridge and exploded while being pursued by the Human Torch. The Crusaders were stripped of the now-useless gear that they had worn with honor and enabled them to be heroes in the defense of their homelands. Captain Wings expressed their thanks to the Invaders for the timely intervention, and how they all felt like fools. Captain America told them to not feel that way since it had been an ingenious scheme that had appealed to their patriotism and how it was a time when most would find it a hard thing to resist such a call to arms.

roger dutton.name: Roger Dutton
roger dutton.origin: When Senator Morton Clegstead backed Project Greenskin to finance with the US erary a high-tech prison to capture Bruce Banner, Dutton opposed him and caused a Congressional hearing in the Capitol Building. Dutton insisted that the investment should be directed to fight poverty or other more useful cause. Project leader General Thaddeus Ross's testimony, justifying Hulkbuster Base as a research area, convinced the Senate to back up Project Greenskin. Dutton nonetheless was authorized to investigate Clegstead himself and, with risk to his life, discovered that Clegstead had personal interests in the project: The Senator was using the Project's resources, without authorization, to fight his own disease and get superhuman powers. Clegstead was killed in combat with the Hulk, but at the same time Dutton got proof of both Clegstead's abuses and of Greenskin's use at medical research. Dutton then went to Ross and told him he had became a supporter of Greenskin.

roger fieldston.origin: Roger had the power to activate latent mutations in anybody he touched and clothing provided no protection. However, the mutations were often severe and grotesque. Roger went to seek out those he had mutated so he could take their powers away.

roger goshaw.name: Roger Goshaw
roger goshaw.first_appearance: Captain America/Nick Fury: Blood Truce Vol 1 1
roger goshaw.origin: Nick Fury recruited Captain America to help locate Dmitri Panshin, a Russian citizen who wished to defect to the United States. Panshin was targeted for assassination by the armored mercenary known as Agent Orange. Captain America found him in Prague, but before he could contact him, Agent Orange burst through the ground and attempted to grab him. Captain America fought Agent Orange, shattering one of his wrist weapons, and Panshin fled again. Captain America caught up with Panshin and his son, Sergei, but the Titanium Man arrived to try to snatch Panshin again. A three-way battle ensued, with Cap and the Titanium Man temporarily flooring Agent Orange, and with the Titanium grabbing Sergei Panshin (as Dmitri had lost himself in the crowd) and flying off. Agent Orange recovered and caught up to the Titanium Man, firing a device that shorted out his armor, forcing him to drop Sergei. Agent Orange grabbed Sergei and escaped.

roger grafton.name: Roger Grafton
roger grafton.origin: Roger Grafton was an explorer who joined Russell and Elaine Simpson on an expedition into the Himalayas in search of the Abominable Snowman. Secretly infatuated with Elaine, Roger saw an opportunity when Russell fell from a cliff and was presumed dead, attempting to persuade Elaine to leave the mountains and return with him. When Russell unexpectedly survived and returned accompanied by Man-Thing, Roger murdered his partner with a gunshot and blamed the killing on the creature. He then tried to force himself upon Elaine and later abandoned her after she injured her ankle during their escape through the mountains. Believing Man-Thing to be the legendary snowman, Roger organized an armed expedition to capture the creature and profit from its discovery. His forces attacked the hidden Himalayan tribe sheltering Elaine and Man-Thing, killing Hiram Swenson during the assault. Roger later attempted to imprison Man-Thing, but the creature escaped and burned Roger’s face upon contact.

roger harrington.name: Roger Harrington
roger harrington.origin: Principal of Midtown High School who first hired Peter Parker as the new Science teacher when the last one left after a student fired upon the occupants of the school. He later also hired Flash Thompson as the School Coach. He followed Spider-Man around during the Mysterio takeover at the school but was told to hide in the A.V Room. Later, after the Mysterios had left, he was killed by the Chameleon from the future in the A.V. Room at Midtown High School, and his appearance was used to employ Peter Parker as the assistant coach.

roger hochberg.name: Roger Hochberg
roger hochberg.origin: Roger was a postgraduate student in the same program Peter Parker followed at Empire State University. He is a shy young man, and so, Peter invited him to a party where Roger was mocked by other students who served him vinegar in a drink. He left the party, but Peter defended him, and after Roger was involved in a fight between Spider-Man and the Red Ghost and his apes, some girls expressed interest in Roger. One of these girls was Mia Carrera, who soon became Roger's girlfriend.

roger joliet.name: Roger Joliet
roger joliet.origin: Roger Joliet teamed up with his employer, Mr. Harlock to steal from the museum. Taking on the identity Jolly Roger, Roger stole from the museum while Harlock acted like he never saw him. Roger found three students wandering about his base, Pirate's Cove but was foiled in his attack by Speedball. During the fight, they broke the Pirate ship which began to sink. Roger seemingly died as he never returned to shore.

roger juniper.name: Roger Juniper
roger juniper.origin: Roger "Buddy" Juniper was one of the S.H.I.E.L.D. agents stationed at the training facility in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba. During an obstacle course, he volunteered to assist Agent 125—Hercules—through the exercise. Hercules took an unconventional approach, toppling a machine gun nest by hurling a mound of dirt at it. As they grew more familiar, Juniper confided that he came from a long line of military service and wanted to honor his family's legacy, even if it meant dying in the field. Hercules responded by recounting the tale of Jason and the Argonauts, warning how their pursuit of glory came at a great cost. Juniper later joined Hercules on a mission to South America, part of a task force targeting a base operated by the Warhawks. By the time they arrived, the Warhawks had abandoned the site, leaving only a Minotaur as a final defense. Juniper attempted to support Hercules in the fight but was fatally struck by the creature. After Hercules defeated the Minotaur, he found Juniper mortally wounded. With his final breath, Juniper asked Hercules to take down Ares for him before passing away.

roger mollech.name: Roger Mollech
roger mollech.origin: Roger Mollech was the corrupt U.S. Attorney General. Along with his aide Angela Stone, he had made a secret alliance with General Miguel Navatilas, dictator of South American country Medisuela. Mollech had access to illegal drugs impounded in the American streets, including cocaine which was imported from Medisuela, then using his authority confiscated them, re-selling them to obtain untraceable funds, with which he bought military weaponry that was then sold or distributed to the Navatilas regime, to equip the Medisuelan National Defense Force Navatilas was to use his more powerful military against neighboring countries (Argentina and Paraguay) whose policies were not favorable to Mollech's and his allies' interests, by fostering insurrection and even arranging coups and going to war - a plan called Project: Democracy. However, Mollech was purposely providing Medisuela with defective weapons that exploded after just a few uses, killing the operator. This was because Mollech's real plan was to pressure the United States government to invade Medisuela, then depose Navatilas and replace him with a puppet government whose strings would be pulled by Mollech himself. To that end, Mollech used his position to damage Navatilas' already weak international public image: Initially supported by the U.S., Navatilas' aggressive policies and alleged crimes caused the General to fall in disfavor. Mollech told Navatilas that he was spending money to improve Navatilas' reputation while ensuring deniability, but Mollech really gave an image as a strong attorney pursuing criminals due to the war on drugs, and putting Navatilas himself in his sights. Mollech also had contact with a rogue element in the American military and law enforcement, the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) led by Colonel Max Kalee, and with several USAF servicemen. Kalee interacted directly with the drug dealers affiliated with the conspiracy, including Doctor Slickster, while Mollech's assistant Stone was the main contact point between him and Navatilas. Their activities however attracted the attention of superhero Captain America, who was notified of an increased weapon traffic by friends in the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms which led him to discover illegal arms sales to the Navatilas regime when the DIA revealed their involvement to salvage the operation (Kalee claimed the DIA would process the criminals and the shipment, not revealing that it would get "lost"); Captain America dug deeper and found not only that the weapons had been sabotaged, but also that the DIA was involved in dirty play, including shipments of weapons to Medisuela using assets from the American government. The conspiracy also got the interest of vigilante the Punisher, who tracked and killed Doctor Slickster, discovering in the process that high-ranking officials were involved. Discovering about both breaches, Stone manipulated the Punisher to make him believe that Captain America was involved in the drug smuggling, so that the Punisher would kill Captain America; she then reported progress to Navatilas and arranged a lunch of Mollech with the President of the United States. The Punisher shot Captain America, but the latter survived and faked his own death to continue the investigation. With TV coverage, Mollech reinforced the Justice Department's commitment to war on drugs, again focusing on Navatilas a s a target, while clandestinely he met with Navatilas on a boat to organize details of the conspiracy; Mollech provided three beautiful young women to Navatilas as a gift before he left - but even then, Mollech, Stone and the DIA were thinking on how to get rid of Navatilas. Soon afterward, Navatilas returned the courtesy by inviting Mollech to a heathen party in Medisuela. Navatilas tried to impress Mollech with a plethora of beautiful women, music and dance, while also trying to find out whether his own decreasing popularity heralded an American invasion on Medisuela; Mollech tried to convince Navatilas that it was a mere deniability tactic. Navatilas then invited Mollech to a ritual where they were to burn a woman alive, so as to arouse other attendees, and the General insisted that Mollech committed the murder. Mollech did not want to get involved in such a crime in his position, but Navatilas insisted that Mollech was to prove his strength to him. Mollech did took the torch to the sacrificial victim; it is inferred that he did kill her. A guest in Medisuela Presidential Palace, Mollech then was phoned by Stone, who told him that enemy forces had found about the weapons sale. Indeed, Captain America and the Punisher had reluctantly formed an alliance and reached Medisuela. However, they triggered a bomb in a camp, the Punisher was believed dead, and Captain America was captured by Medisuelan Colonel Antonio Veneno. roger norvell.name: Roger Norvell
roger norvell.origin: thumb|left|207px Roger "Red" Norvell joined Harris Hobbs' film crew along with Joey Burnett to document the real-life Norse Gods. But Thor refused to help Harris even after hearing of his visions of himself and the Midgard Serpent. With his plans lost, Loki, who had been listening, offered to help. When Thor was transferring a large adamantium computer from Stark International to Asgard for safe keeping, Loki distracted Thor with an illusion of Jormungand while Red and the others hid in a compartment. Loki and Hela planned to bring about Volla's prediction of Ragnarök and not only wanted the film crew to film his victory but Harris' visions played a part in this prediction. While filming Red noticed Lady Sif and was infatuated. Red made his move but Sif brutally rebuked his advances. In anger, Red walked off only to be met by a watching Loki. Loki promised that Red could become as powerful as Thor and gain the affection of Sif if he would come with him. Loki brought Red to where his monsters waited to attack Asgard, and there he had Red film his victory, but thanks to Sif, who learned of Loki's doings, Thor arrived. The two fought but with the Axe of Odin Loki had the edge, until Thor summoned his Megingjord (Belt of Strength), and, with Loki's army defeated, Thor flew them back to Asgard. Once there he handed his belt to Red to hold, but Loki told Red that he should take the belt to the Palace of Thor in Bilskirnir. Once there, Red walked through the Fires of Geirrodur to acquire the Iron Gloves of Thor. thumb|left|206px As Odin laid judgment on Loki, Red, who succeed in the trial, donned the Belt of Strength as well as the Iron Gloves and gained the powers of Thor. Red then challenged Thor and claimed Mjolnir, with which he defeated Thor. Red was going to kill Thor until Joey sacrificed himself to save Thor. Shocked by what he did and promising not to kill Thor or anyone else if Sif came with him, the two left Asgard for Alfheim. Once at Alfheim, Red drove off the Bright-Elves (Ljos-Alfar). Sif told him that Odin, in case Thor would exhaust strength protecting Earth or be absent, had created the process to ensure that there could always be a Thor to protect Asgard. He placed the powers and essence of Thor into his gloves, belt, and the Fire of Geirrodur, and once a lesser godling or mortals had the essence of Thor, they would have a special affinity for Mjolnir. In Asgard, Hela attacked with an army of monsters. Thor battled Jormungand, but without Mjolnir, Thor stood no chance until Red with Sif arrived. Red took on the serpent, and due to not being experienced with Mjolnir he tossed it to Thor. As Thor fought back Hela's monsters Red beat down Jormungand, wounding it and drawing it back, then sacrificed himself to hold it back. With Red dead, Thor brought his body to where Joey's had been laying and Harris, who mourned the loss of his friends. It was then revealed that Odin had not only created the means for another Thor to be birthed to protect Asgard, but had also set these events in motion in order to thwart Ragnarok by replacing his son with another. Though Red's body was brought back to Earth, his spirit was sent to Valhalla. ===Replaced in Asgard by another Thor=== Red had seemingly been forgotten about, save for an interview by Madelyn Arnstein of his old friend and boss Harris Hobbs. But Odin had not forgotten Red. With Thor constantly ignoring his responsibilities to Asgard in choosing to stay on Earth, and Asgard in need of a Thor due to the looming Ragnarok, Odin could think of no one better then Roger Norvell. Odin traveled to Valhalla to retrieve Red as the new Thor, much to Red's shock. Red put the Iron Gloves and Belt of Strength on and became Thor once again. With his own War-Hammer and Odin adopting him as his son, they journeyed back to Asgard. When Thor returned to Asgard angry with Odin and in search for the truth of Donald Blake, Red took offense and stepped in. Odin stopped them, and as he retold how he created the means for another Thor to come to be to protect Asgard all those years ago. But that he also did it to have a thunder God fulfil the prophecy of Ragnar, and be slain so his son might live. How his heart was sad, that Thor brought home the body of the other and knowing that he had deliberately set it in motion. Odin then revealed how Red came to be Thor once again, and declared that since bring Red back he has no other sons. Once done Odin told Thor to leave Asgard, but when he refused until he got answers about Blake, Red decided to make him leave. As they battled, all of Asgard shook while Odin, Sif, Balder, Beta Ray Bill and the Warriors Three watched. With Odin's Palace falling apart and the Rainbow Bridge violently vibrating, Odin stopped the fight. Odin told them of the secrets of Blake and the wars fought as well. In the end Odin once again declared Red his son and that he'd be Thor of Asgard and with that Thor Odinson left for Earth. thumb|left|204px ===Myth Conce

Odin traveled to Valhalla to retrieve Red as the new Thor, much to Red's shock. Red put the Iron Gloves and Belt of Strength on and became Thor once again. With his own War-Hammer and Odin adopting him as his son, they journeyed back to Asgard. When Thor returned to Asgard angry with Odin and in search for the truth of Donald Blake, Red took offense and stepped in. Odin stopped them, and as he retold how he created the means for another Thor to come to be to protect Asgard all those years ago. But that he also did it to have a thunder God fulfil the prophecy of Ragnar, and be slain so his son might live. How his heart was sad, that Thor brought home the body of the other and knowing that he had deliberately set it in motion. Odin then revealed how Red came to be Thor once again, and declared that since bring Red back he has no other sons. Once done Odin told Thor to leave Asgard, but when he refused until he got answers about Blake, Red decided to make him leave. As they battled, all of Asgard shook while Odin, Sif, Balder, Beta Ray Bill and the Warriors Three watched. With Odin's Palace falling apart and the Rainbow Bridge violently vibrating, Odin stopped the fight. Odin told them of the secrets of Blake and the wars fought as well. In the end Odin once again declared Red his son and that he'd be Thor of Asgard and with that Thor Odinson left for Earth. thumb|left|204px ===Myth Conce

Red was noted to have a rage equal to that of Odin's by Odin himself. When Red became mortal again he briefly dated Sabrina which he nicknamed Breena or Breenie, who unbeknownst to him was married to Johnny the Gent. A known criminal in the communities of New Jersey where Red was living. In all the time Red possessed his own war-hammer a copy of Mjolnir he never officially gave it a name, just referred to the War-Hammer as Enchanted Mallet or Magic Hammer. roger phillips.name: Roger Phillips
roger phillips.origin: Rogers was an accomplished gymnast who was hired by Spymaster to join his Espionage Elite. Rogers and the Espionage Elite aided Spymaster in breaking into Stark Industries in order to steal its secrets. They came into conflict with Iron Man, Mike O'Brien, and some security guards and were eventually defeated with Spymaster abandoning the team. Rogers and the team were later reunited by Spymaster in order to hack Iron Man's armor. However, the hacker Spymaster hired, Glitch, chose to turn on the team, allowing the Espionage Elite to be captured. Spymaster escaped but was later captured. When the Espionage Elite, no longer working for Spymaster, planned a heist at Avengers Mansion, Godfried Herter betrayed the team, planning to take all the money for himself. He reprogrammed the Avengers Training System to target and kill anyone carrying his uniquely built phone, managing to kill both Phillips and Farley London before Wasp stopped him.

roger sharmine.name: Roger Sharmine
roger sharmine.origin: thumb|left|83px|Roger Sharmine Roger Sharmine was an electrical engineer who by 1946 had founded the Sharmine Electrical Society to help bring advancements to electrical sciences. He developed a "Green-Out" generator, a device that created a thick green luminescent fog that blinded those who were caught in it, and a means to see through it. Adopting the name Amkenon he formed a gang that dressed and used ancient Egyptian symbolism as a means of confusing the public as to the nature of his Green-Out device. He revealed his true identity to at least one other member a man named Mongrel. Activating the device remotely from his hideout Amkenon and his men committed several lucrative and daring robberies, attracting the attention of the Sub-Mariner when they robbed cruise ship. When Namor tried to stop them he was blinded by their the Green-Out and was knocked out. However as Amkenon and his men fled, a crate fell on one of his minions and they left him for dead. This eventually proved to be Amkenon's undoing, as this man also knew his true identity and provided part of Sharmine's last name before dying. When Namor learned of the Sharmine Electrical Society, he paid them a visit. There he confronted Roger Sharmine and found that his pocket watch had the same dragon emblem that Amkenon's gang wore on their armor. Roger then made up a story, telling him that his "brother" Arnold, a practitioner of mysticism obtained the "Green-Out" device, really a mystical artifact, after rescuing the daughter of an Egyptian priest and then began using it for crime. Roger was then had his men stage a "kidnapping" using the Green-Out to escape. Back in his uniform, Amkenon was about to murder Mongrel for letting his identity slip when Namor, having tracked the gang down, smashed into their base. Once more blinded by the Green-Out, Namor and Mongrel were knocked out and left in the basement of the hideout to be blown up by a time-bomb while Amkenon and his men committed their next crime. Namor and Mongrel managed to escape the hideout before the bomb went off. The explosion uncovered the secret bunker where the electrical generator that created the Green-Out was hidden. Namor destroyed it, causing the Green-Out effect to fade away and Amkenon and his gang were quickly arrested. Arriving on the scene, Namor unmasked Amkenon revealing him to be Roger Sharmine, who confessed that the story about his "brother" was false, before he was turned over to the authorities. Sharmine's subsequent fate is unknown.

roger stevens.origin: ===Early Life=== left|thumb|Steve Rogers in his childhood Steve Rogers was born September 28, 1922, to poor Irish, Christian, immigrant parents, Sarah and Joseph Rogers. He grew up a frail youth during the Great Depression in New York City. His tonsils were removed at the age of seven, being the only important surgery in his life; he also suffered from chicken pox, measles and mumps. A strong sense of duty and honor was instilled in him due to the moral influence of both parents. Rogers' father died when he was a child, and his mother died from pneumonia later, when he was in his late teens. thumb|right|150px|Steve Rogers before Operation: Rebirth Moving into a rooming house and taking a job as a delivery boy, Steve struggled to survive. Growing up as a child, Steve was constantly picked on by other children due to his frail and sickly body. As a young child Steve attended a school in the Lower East Side neighborhood, where patriotic values to bring freedom and justice to all were instilled in him through people like his his civics teacher. Steve had a love for drawing, and later became an art student, even winning contest awards. Not giving up his love of drawing, he once won the gold medal in the Creative Arts annual "Art of the Future" contest. ===Project Rebirth=== Seeking an escape from his ever day life, Steve enjoyed going to the movies. One day in the fall of 1940, he was horrified by newsreels about the Nazi's invasion of Europe and atrocities in Asia that the Empire of Japan committed in China and Korea and became determined to join the army in order to do his part to protect America from the potential Nazi threat. In the Fall of 1940 Sam Fogler convinced Steve to travel to Los Angeles in order to find his brother who had moved out west and then lost contact with him. On November 15, 1940 Sam found his brother, Harold, and attempted to convince him to leave his life of crime. They were caught by the members of Harold's gang who were revealed to be Nazis. After Steve called the gang "Nazi scum" and "hateful monsters" the leader didn't shoot him as he was a "weakling" but instead killed "the strong one," Sam. After the police apprehended the Nazis Steve was told that his actions from that night were proof he had the heart to fight in the war. Steve then began volunteering to join the United States military, but due to his frail body he was was rejected under class 4-F, making him ineligible to become a soldier. During one such occasion, Steve was forced to evade Nazi spies. After his latest rejection for military service, Steve's devotion to serving his country attracted the attention of General Chester Phillips who offered Steve an opportunity to help. This opportunity was Project Rebirth, a secret military project to create a breed of super soldiers. Following his acceptance into the project, Steve met with the creator of the Super-Soldier Serum, scientist Abraham Erskine. Steve then underwent initial tests and met project member Cynthia Glass who was, unknown to him, a Nazi spy. When Nazis attempted to attack the secret base, Steve was protected by Dominic Fortune, a soldier of fortune who was originally a candidate for the project but was turned down due to his questionable lifestyle. thumb|150px|left|Steve Rogers' transformation into Captain America In the winter of 1940 the final preparations were made and Steve Rogers underwent the final test. He was injected and made to ingest Erskine's formula and then was bathed in Vita Rays which caused his body to transform into the peak of human perfection. By this time, the project was infiltrated by Nazi agent Heinz Kruger who fatally shot Erskine, Kruger himself was slain by the newly empowered Steve Rogers. Without any complete copies of the super-soldier formula available in Erskine's writing, Steve Rogers was the only man to receive the complete treatment at that time. Soon after, an attempt by Nazi spies to steal a urine sample from Steve Rogers was foiled. ===Becoming Captain America=== After saying goodbye to his childhood friend Arnie Roth, Steve began a battery of training to hone his fighting skills and military strategy. He trained with the most skilled and elite athletes — including the greatest boxers, wrestlers, bodybuilders, gymnasts — as well as the best military strategists and other instructors, who taught him gymnastics, hand-to-hand combat, military strategy, and tactics, all under the supervision of General Phillips. During this time, General Phillips located a journal belonging to Steve's ancestor who lived during the American Revolution. This ancestor was a hero who wore an American themed costume and operated under the name Captain America. The military decided to model Steve after his ancestors other identity. By March of 1941, Steve Roger's learned of his polar opposite - the Nazi Red Skull. It was shortly after this that Steve was given his American flag themed uniform. fields.personality: Captain America is extremely selfless, brave, and determined to stand up for what is right no matter how difficult the situations. He is traditionally seen as one of the greatest heroes in the universe. He is a righteous and brave man who always wanted to see the good in people. From even before his origins as a super hero, Steve has always devoted himself to the protection of the weak and the defense of freedom and justice. Captain America's extremely selflessness is not just in his actions but also in his willingness to make difficult decisions for the greater good, often grappling with the moral complexities of war and leadership. His self-sacrificial nature is central to his identity, making him one of the most iconic and virtuous characters in the Marvel Universe. As an exemplary instance of Captain America's extreme selflessness is when he attends an anti-Nazi protest, where tensions escalate between demonstrators and neo-Nazis. Amid the chaos, Captain America intervenes by delivering a powerful speech about the importance of free speech and the horrors of the Holocaust, drawing from his own experiences as a liberator during World War II. He confronts the neo-Nazi leaders with firsthand accounts of liberation, stating, "I wish I could take you back with me to the day we liberated Diebenwald—let you smell the stomach-turning stench of death—let you see the mountains of corpses left behind by the corrupt madmen and murderers you idolize." This moment not only highlights his unwavering commitment to justice but also reveals his identity to the public, showcasing his readiness to sacrifice personal anonymity for the greater good. His unwavering commitment to truth and justice in the face of hate and violence underscores his extreme selflessness. This act exemplifies his extremely selfless character, as he consistently places the needs of others above his own, even when it involves personal risk and the potential loss of his secret identity. His dedication to moral principles, even when faced with personal risk, highlights his role as a steadfast symbol of virtue and courage. In spite of his virtues, however, Cap has been plagued by his status as man out of time. Remembering his days as a soldier in World War II, Cap worried that his idealism might be considered outdated in the modern world. Furthermore, seeing how idealized his legacy has become throughout the years, Cap sometimes believed that he might not be able to fulfill the image the world had of him. Regardless, Cap is still seen as the pinnacle of heroism and an example for everyone to follow. One of the most defining moments of Steve Rogers' character comes occurs during the events of Fear Itself, when he boldly stands up to Odin, who is the All-Father and king of the Asgardian gods and commands him to heal a dying Thor with absolute authority and unfathomable determination, who had just survived a brutal battle with the Hulk, possessed by the Serpent's power as the monstrous Nul, Breaker of Worlds. After giving everything he had to stop the rampaging force, Thor collapses from his injuries, broken and on the edge of death. With Earth on the brink of destruction and its heroes scattered or broken, Steve steps forward, not with brute strength or godly power, but with unwavering moral conviction. He confronts Odin not as an equal in power, but as an equal in principle demanding that the All-Father stop abandoning humanity and take responsibility for the chaos unleashed. What makes this moment extraordinary is that Steve shows no hesitation. Despite Odin's vast power, Steve doesn't flinch. He doesn't ask for help, he demands justice, protection, and accountability. It's not rebellion for its own sake; it's a fearless defense of what's right. In doing so, Steve embodies the highest form of heroism, not in action alone, but in standing firm against impossible odds when no one else will. This confrontation is not just about saving Earth, it's about character. Steve Rogers proves that true courage doesn't come from powers or titles. It comes from the moral strength to speak truth to power, the heart to defend the defenseless, and the determination to fight for what's right, no matter the cost. Captain America believes in the freedom that everyone should be free to achieve their full potential. He wants people to become the best person they can be while fulfilling their American Dream. His view of American Dream is to help make the country the place where it is possible, to inspire by example, and to enable everyone's American dreams. According to Nick Fury, Rogers fought for his country during its greatest and darkest time. He inspired people when inspiration is necessary. Steve Rogers had to endure the changes that is happening in the world, and he is preserved the only way he knows how by being a hero. He represents everything great about America at the same time, he represents some of its flaws. Steve Rogers will always fight for what is right. He wo

fields.notes: Due to his connection to the events in World War II and subsequent suspended animation, Cap is one of the few characters whose backstory isn't affected by Marvel's Sliding Timescale. Captain America's official membership status in the Avengers charter has been subject to revision. Initially, he was considered the team's first recruit after the founders, and was reported as such in many publications. The Avengers Charter, published in , was signed by the Hulk and the other founders, not Cap. In , Iron Man also "pulled rank" on Captain America on Hala, claiming to be the "only founding member present". Beginning with , however, the idea of Captain America being a "retroactive founder" of the Avengers was put forth, allegedly replacing the Hulk in official documents as a founding member in order to ensure the team's good name was properly upheld. went further and stated this retroactive founder status was established behind-the-scenes in the early days of the Avengers, prior to . Joe Simon initially considered calling his new character "Super American". He quickly changed it to "Captain America", arguing that there were too many "Supers" and not a lot of "Captains" in comics. In 1996's DC vs. Marvel, fought against Captain America. Their fight was a draw until the sewer where they were fighting got flooded. The current knocked both combatants off-balance, causing Cap's shield to miss his opponent whereas Batman managed to hit Steve's head with a batarang and knock him out. In the same series, Captain America defeated , who is known for crippling Bruce Wayne. Batman acknowledged in the JLA/Avengers crossover that it is possible Captain America could beat him, but it would take him a very long time.
fields.trivia: Steve Rogers has been shown to be worthy of wielding Mjolnir. Rogers has at times owned the copyright to the Captain America Uniform and even threatened to take legal action against U.S.Agent when he wore a version of it without his permission. He is one of few people capable of accessing Iron Man's armory, and is one of two foreigners entrusted with the Black Panther's technology. At the Pentagon, Captain America was granted a Paladin-Plus Clearance. Steve has done some pencil work for Marvel Comics where he drew some of his own adventures for them, as he is listed as the penciler for . Steve Rogers is one of the few people that Deadpool truly respects, due to Captain America being Wade's childhood hero. Since both gained their abilities as a result of experimentation, Rogers empathizes with Wade, and is one of the few heroes shown to genuinely like the Merc with a Mouth. Nick Fury's intel classified Rogers as power level 8. Steve favors . His favorite food, as provided by Jarvis, include American cheese on whole wheat, with a glass of milk. Steve is a fan of . Steve Rogers personally hates tattoos. Captain America's favorite romantic comedy is . Emma Frost reminds Steve of his mother. Captain America was merged with two DC characters, and to create Super-Soldier, and Captain America Jr, respectively. In , two halves of Captain America merged with the halves of Hulk and Silver Surfer to create Captain Cosmos and Major Gamma. Captain America was ranked 6th on IGN's "Top 100 Comic Book Heroes of All Time" in 2011. Captain America was ranked 2nd in "The Top 50 Avengers" in 2012. Captain America was also ranked 2nd on IGN's "Top 25 Best Marvel Superheroes" in 2014. Captain America was one of the characters featured in Series A of the Marvel Value Stamps issued in the 1970s.

roger tyson.name: Roger Tyson
roger tyson.species: Human mutated from exposure to chemicals
roger tyson.origin: Milwaukee-born Roger Tyson was a chemist with a background to identify and to study controlled substances and an aspiring stand-up comedian - but lacking any skill for this later career. Tyson began working in a chemical research firm, suddenly disappearing in 1989 along with a number of controlled drugs, including experimental pain-killing drugs. At the same time, the serial killer the Harlequin made his first appearance, dressed as a medieval jester with a domino mask and bright gaudy blue slippers with curled toes and bells. For ten days, the Harlequin murdered several people, slashing their throats ear-to-ear and dropping them from rooftops. He was eventually apprehended by local heroes from Madison, Wisconsin. His defense was that the victims were not laughing at his jokes, so he "made them laugh" via . The Harlequin was sent to the Mendotta Mental Health Institute, where he was identified as Roger Tyson - but the Harlequin refused to answer to this name. He was diagnosed as a schizophrenic paranoid with persistent fantasy identity. During his 8-month stay at the Mental Health Institute, the Harlequin's body mutated, developing his powers and muscles, and also changing his cosmetic appearance in a way that, except seen closely, was perceived as make-up. Doctors Mathus and Rachel Echaus in the Mental Health Institute concluded that the Harlequin was not a mutant but had been changed due to exposure to chemical mutagens; not knowing which chemicals in particular, they could not hope to reverse the changes. While in hospital, Dr. Edgar Josephs treated the Harlequin, diagnosing that the source of Tyson's problems was a lack of self-awareness of reality. The Harlequin was unhappy at Josephs' failing to understand the Harlequin's comedy-based philosophy. Eventually, the Harlequin drove Josephs crazy due to constant contact. Josephs helped Harlequin escape, then became a patient in the same hospital. The Harlequin started a new rampage with a different uniform - A white dinner jacket and tails over a black spandex jogging suit and neon blue stripe running up the right side of his outfit while keeping his previous uniform's shoes. He also included lethal gadgets in his suits. After rampages throughout all of the country, the Harlequin was again apprehended and returned to the Mental Health Institute, where he was kept under physical restraints, including a straight-jacket. Dr. Echaus replaced Dr. Josephs as the Harlequin's therapist. In her first interview and observation, on October 13th, 1990, Echaus noticed the Harlequin's disturbing features. The Harlequin was not cooperative, instead replying with sexual innuendos, limericks, and mock romantic approaches. He mentioned Dr. Josephs, hoping that Echaus would be a better company, and also a then-recently deceased person called Roger. Echaus noticed the lack of progress and decided to keep the Harlequin under restraints.

fields.notes: The Harlequin was created by Steven E. Schend for the article "With Great Power" (subtitled "Hey - This Next One'll Kill Ya!"), for the role-playing game Polyhedron #58 (1991), as a Non-Player Character villain for TSR, Inc.'s Marvel Super Heroes Role-Playing Game. The magazine's cover included an illustration of the Harlequin by Andrew Ellis. This was the only Marvel-related article in Polyhedron. The Harlequin appears to be a pastiche of the DC Comics villain . Both have similar origins: they were struggling comedians whose appearances were altered by chemicals, causing them to go insane and killing people on impulse while also using clown-themed gadgets.

roger white.name: Roger White
roger white.origin: Roger White was a boy who was teased by his peers because he was fearful, and above all he was afraid of heights and therefore he did not accept any challenge that involved courage, and for this reason they called him a coward. When his parents had to leave, he told him to invite his friend Ned Brooks to stay with him and to check on a building that used to be part of a factory he owned. Ned accepted the invitation and together they decided to visit the building, but once they climbed up to the roof, the door on the roof locked with the keys in the lock inside. Ned tried to take a rope from a flagpole, but fell and broke his arm. Roger then, even though he was in the grip of fear, he pulled himself together and lowered himself with the rope taken from Ned from the building going to call for help for his injured friend.

roglo.name: Roglo
roglo.origin: Roglo was a crooked politician that had many criminal dealings. He operated out of one of New York's slums. Despite his criminal activities being known to authorities, they had no proof against him to do anything about it. That is, until the android Human Torch joined the police force. When the Torch began working the beat in Roglo's neighborhood, he called the Torch up to his office and try to tell him to stay out of his business. When the Torch refused, Roglo and his minion Red attempted to rough him up; however, the Torch's flame powers allowed him to get away. Noticing that the Torch left his police hat behind, Roglo called the police station, pretending to be a good Samaritan wanting to return it. When the Human Torch went to retrieve his hat, he walked into a trap set by Roglo. While the Torch was left to Red to dispose of, Roglo headed off to burn down a recently insured building that he owned so he could collect on the insurance. As he prepared the building to burn, Red came to him warning of the Torch's escape. Roglo shot Red in cold blood for his failure. When the Torch attempted to stop Roglo, the crooked politician tossed kerosene on the Torch, temporarily knocking him out from the explosion and setting the building ablaze. The Torch revived and learned from the dying Red of Roglo's plot. The Torch put out the blaze and then stopped Roglo and his remaining minions from escaping. Upon capture, Roglo surrendered, agreeing to give a complete confession to the police.

rognar.name: Rognar
rognar.origin: Rognar was a Northman king that led his men on the Viking path. They came to Britain where they pillaged and burned villages, until they were trapped by Bran Mak Morn while pillaging a Pict village. The Pictish king spared them in return for their oath of fighting one battle for him, against Rome. When he died from a Roman arrow, his men, represented by Wulfhere, after having drunk the mead of council and spoke to their fire, considered that they were absolved of the oath as it had been sworn under Rognar, and stated they would join Bran Mak Morn only if he provided a king for them, or else they would join the Romans. Bran Mak Morn finally benefited from those men's support, when Gonar pulled from the past King Kull of Valusia, who slew Wulfhere in duel and earned the Northmen's respect and leadership.

rogue anna marie.name: Rogue (Anna Marie)
rogue anna marie.origin: ===Girl on the Run=== left|thumb|Young Anna Marie and her mother Anna Marie was born to Priscilla and Owen in a back-to-nature hippie commune in Caldecott County, Mississippi. She was delivered by her aunt Carrie, her mother's sister. Although the prude Carrie believed Owen had ruined Priscilla's life, she still maintained a relationship with Priscilla and Anna Marie, who frequently visited her in their family's ancestral farmhouse. However, after Carrie reprimanded Priscilla for sharing the commune's attempt to use Native American mysticism to reach an ethereal plane known as the Far Banks, the sisters cut ties with each other. The ritual resulted in Priscilla's disappearance. Owen informed Carrie about the incident and left Anna Marie under her care while asking her to move in to the commune, which she refused. In her grief at the loss of her sister, Carrie proved to be a strict and authoritarian guardian to protect her niece. This led Anna Marie to be a rebellious child. Her poor relationship with her rigid aunt and distant father prompted her to run away from home as a kid. Fending for herself as a loner, the young girl was nicknamed by the locals as "Rogue", which became the only name she would go by. The skittish Rogue was approached by a warm-hearted Mystique, a mutant shapeshifter. Since Mystique was an outcast herself, Rogue trusted her. Mystique took Rogue in on the advice of her precognitive partner, Destiny. As part of a family, Rogue enjoyed happy moments with her mothers. However, due to Destiny's knowledge about the future, Mystique was secretly aware of Rogue's condition as a mutant and, in fact, had plans of using Rogue in her mission as a mutant terrorist. At some point, Rogue grew close to a boy named Cody Robbins. Mystique feared for their relationship, wishing to prevent any development from it. Still, during their flirtation, Rogue impulsively kissed Robbins, at which point her latent mutant power to absorb the life energy and psyche of others with skin-to-skin contact emerged. Cody Robbins was left in a coma from which he would not awaken. Rogue was traumatized by the experience, breaking her spirit to the point of embracing Mystique's mission. Not able to control her absorption powers at first, Rogue usually wore body-concealing clothing that eliminated the possibility of accidental skin contact. Now having powers, Rogue was introduced by Mystique to crime as part of her Brotherhood of Evil Mutants. Soon, in their secret missions, Rogue realized how dreadful her powers could be as she shared her mind with those she acted against through touch. ===Ms. Marvel=== One of Destiny's visions predicted that the super-heroine Carol Danvers, the mighty Ms. Marvel, would ruin Rogue's life. In order to protect Rogue, Mystique had her Brotherhood attack Ms. Marvel with no success, leading to their arrest. Noticing Mystique's fury, Rogue decided to deal with their enemy by herself in secrecy. Learning Ms. Marvel would be in San Francisco, Rogue tackled her, wishing to prove her worth to the eyes of the Brotherhood. During a fight at the Golden Gate Bridge, Rogue's powers interacted with Ms. Marvel in an unexpected way: Rogue absorbed Ms. Marvel's alien-based powers and memories permanently. Rogue gained Ms. Marvel's incredible strength, near-invulnerability, the power of flight, but her psyche was fractured in the process, ironically consummating Destiny's prediction. Rogue disposed of the apparently lifeless body of Danvers, who was saved by Spider-Woman. Rogue's loneliness, envy, bitterness, and despair turned into anger. Wielding Ms. Marvel's abilities, she was ordered to defeat the Avengers, attacking them at their mansion headquarters in order to acquire enough power to break the arrested Brotherhood members free. Rogue was able to incapacitate Captain America and Thor, but was forced to retreat for not being able to subdue Wonder Man with her absorption powers. After regrouping with the Brotherhood at the prison on Ryker's Island, Rogue battled the Avengers one more time. The Avengers prevailed, prompting Mystique to escape with Rogue. Danvers was psychically treated by the telepath Professor Charles Xavier of the mutant group known as the X-Men, adversaries of Mystique and the Brotherhood. Unbeknownst to them, Mystique had secretly set base at the Pentagon. When Danvers and the X-Men Storm and Wolverine invaded the Pentagon to delete data they had on the X-Men, Rogue was casually seen by her victim. Danvers immediately unleashed her rage upon her aggressor, but Rogue proved to be a formidable foe, forcing Storm to send her out of the battle site with a cyclone. ===Sisterhood of Evil Mutants=== Soon after, Mystique and Rogue envisioned a plan to free their teammates from the Windust Maximum Security Prison. fields.history: ===Girl on the Run=== left|thumb|Young Anna Marie and her mother Anna Marie was born to Priscilla and Owen in a back-to-nature hippie commune in Caldecott County, Mississippi. She was delivered by her aunt Carrie, her mother's sister. Although the prude Carrie believed Owen had ruined Priscilla's life, she still maintained a relationship with Priscilla and Anna Marie, who frequently visited her in their family's ancestral farmhouse. However, after Carrie reprimanded Priscilla for sharing the commune's attempt to use Native American mysticism to reach an ethereal plane known as the Far Banks, the sisters cut ties with each other. The ritual resulted in Priscilla's disappearance. Owen informed Carrie about the incident and left Anna Marie under her care while asking her to move in to the commune, which she refused. In her grief at the loss of her sister, Carrie proved to be a strict and authoritarian guardian to protect her niece. This led Anna Marie to be a rebellious child. Her poor relationship with her rigid aunt and distant father prompted her to run away from home as a kid. Fending for herself as a loner, the young girl was nicknamed by the locals as "Rogue", which became the only name she would go by. The skittish Rogue was approached by a warm-hearted Mystique, a mutant shapeshifter. Since Mystique was an outcast herself, Rogue trusted her. Mystique took Rogue in on the advice of her precognitive partner, Destiny. As part of a family, Rogue enjoyed happy moments with her mothers. However, due to Destiny's knowledge about the future, Mystique was secretly aware of Rogue's condition as a mutant and, in fact, had plans of using Rogue in her mission as a mutant terrorist. At some point, Rogue grew close to a boy named Cody Robbins. Mystique feared for their relationship, wishing to prevent any development from it. Still, during their flirtation, Rogue impulsively kissed Robbins, at which point her latent mutant power to absorb the life energy and psyche of others with skin-to-skin contact emerged. Cody Robbins was left in a coma from which he would not awaken. Rogue was traumatized by the experience, breaking her spirit to the point of embracing Mystique's mission. Not able to control her absorption powers at first, Rogue usually wore body-concealing clothing that eliminated the possibility of accidental skin contact. Now having powers, Rogue was introduced by Mystique to crime as part of her Brotherhood of Evil Mutants. Soon, in their secret missions, Rogue realized how dreadful her powers could be as she shared her mind with those she acted against through touch. ===Ms. Marvel=== One of Destiny's visions predicted that the super-heroine Carol Danvers, the mighty Ms. Marvel, would ruin Rogue's life. In order to protect Rogue, Mystique had her Brotherhood attack Ms. Marvel with no success, leading to their arrest. Noticing Mystique's fury, Rogue decided to deal with their enemy by herself in secrecy. Learning Ms. Marvel would be in San Francisco, Rogue tackled her, wishing to prove her worth to the eyes of the Brotherhood. During a fight at the Golden Gate Bridge, Rogue's powers interacted with Ms. Marvel in an unexpected way: Rogue absorbed Ms. Marvel's alien-based powers and memories permanently. Rogue gained Ms. Marvel's incredible strength, near-invulnerability, the power of flight, but her psyche was fractured in the process, ironically consummating Destiny's prediction. Rogue disposed of the apparently lifeless body of Danvers, who was saved by Spider-Woman. Rogue's loneliness, envy, bitterness, and despair turned into anger.
