fields.notes: The exact chronology of Rogue's origins have been revisited more than once. In , Rogue first mentions how her powers activated when she touched Cody Robbins, prompting her to run away. It was not explicit whether or not she had already been taken in by Mystique by then. The story in which Rogue touches Cody Robbins is explored in detail in . In this story, Rogue was already Mystique's protégée even before her powers had activated. Robbins is erroneously named "Freddy" in this story, a mistake that was explained in as Rogue's own confusion about the situation. In , Mystique approached Rogue after her powers had already manifested by having touched Robbins. It is stated that Rogue had run away due to having harmed Robbins. The events depicted in contradict Robbins' condition portrayed in . Originally, Robbins was momentarily stunned by Rogue's contact while in later stories he never woke up from the coma she had put him in. In , Rogue states Mystique was the one who baptized her with her mutant name. Rogue was seen in being lynched by a mob who attacked her in response to Robbins' coma. It was not revealed whether she had already met Mystique by that moment or not. According to Operation Zero Tolerance's Rogue sub-file 100349, after her powers manifested, she was attacked by a monster calling itself "Rogue", who absorbed her and took her appearance. The story reported in the file is only compatible with the interpretation of the events in which Mystique met Rogue after the incident with Robbins. However, the files, as represented in , are usually considered to be false, with the purpose of misleading the X-Men. With the revelation of Rogue's biological family in , it was revealed that what drove her out of her own home as a fugitive was her relationship with her aunt. In the most recent depiction of her origins, in , Mystique met a prepubescent Rogue due to Destiny's recommendation, arguing Rogue would fall into the hands of ill-intended manipulators. In this scenario, it seems unlikely that Rogue had already had her powers activated and her status as a mutant was only known due to Destiny's predictive powers. Steve Rogers considered that Rogue would be a great asset to any team as leader or second-in-command, and would benefit teams of new generation heroes like the Runaways or the Young Masters, and that she would be the perfect candidate to lead the Thunderbolts if Luke Cage was to step down from that position. He would later make her leader of the Avengers Unity Division.
fields.trivia: upright=1.2|thumb|right|In her 4th appearance, Rogue kisses Rom, and in doing so, absorbs more than just his powers. The first time it was suggested that Rogue could turn good was in Rom #32, where the mutant kisses the Spaceknight known as Rom in an attempt to steal his powers, but ends up absorbing his courage and heroism. While the effect is of course temporary, experiencing these emotions (perhaps for the first time) leaves an imprint on Rogue that becomes one of her biggest inspirations to correct her path and subsequently join the X-Men. Writers Bill Mantlo (Rom) and Chris Claremont (Uncanny X-Men) collaborated frequently during the 80's, so it's quite possible that it was Mantlo who originally proposed the idea of ​​redeeming Rogue, and then Claremont played along. Likewise, there's also the possibility that Claremont had already conceived the concept beforehand, and Mantlo, knowing his future intentions for the character, simply decided to implement the first hints in Roms pages. The briefly hinted romance between Rogue and Rom was never revisited. Rogue is known as "Malicia" in French, "Titania" in Latin American Spanish, "Pícara" in European Spanish, "Vampira" in Portuguese, "Шельма" in Russian (also "Руж" in X-Men: Evolution and Wolverine and the X-Men), Vadóc in Hungarian, and was known as "Parasit" in Danish and "Ruda" in Polish. The issue in which Rogue joins the X-Men was voted the 49th greatest Marvel Comic of all time. Rogue was #5 on IGN's Top Twenty-Five X-Men list, and #4 on their Top Ten X-Babes list and #3 on Marvel's list of Top 10 Toughest Females for 2009 and was given title of #1 X-Man on CBR's Top 50 X-Men of All Time for 2008. Depending on the writer, Rogue's dialogue usually has 'I' replaced with 'Ah' to emphasize her southern accent. This is not the case all the time, however. Rogue reflects the stereotype of a southern belle, a woman in the South who is beautiful, flirtatious, yet chaste. Rogue's absorption of Genis-Vell's cosmic powers during was meant to be a long-lasting consequence of House of M; however, the X-Men-related books weren't interested in following this plot point, so the power upgrade only lasted as long as House of M.

In this scenario, it seems unlikely that Rogue had already had her powers activated and her status as a mutant was only known due to Destiny's predictive powers. Steve Rogers considered that Rogue would be a great asset to any team as leader or second-in-command, and would benefit teams of new generation heroes like the Runaways or the Young Masters, and that she would be the perfect candidate to lead the Thunderbolts if Luke Cage was to step down from that position. He would later make her leader of the Avengers Unity Division.
fields.trivia: upright=1.2|thumb|right|In her 4th appearance, Rogue kisses Rom, and in doing so, absorbs more than just his powers. The first time it was suggested that Rogue could turn good was in Rom #32, where the mutant kisses the Spaceknight known as Rom in an attempt to steal his powers, but ends up absorbing his courage and heroism. While the effect is of course temporary, experiencing these emotions (perhaps for the first time) leaves an imprint on Rogue that becomes one of her biggest inspirations to correct her path and subsequently join the X-Men. Writers Bill Mantlo (Rom) and Chris Claremont (Uncanny X-Men) collaborated frequently during the 80's, so it's quite possible that it was Mantlo who originally proposed the idea of ​​redeeming Rogue, and then Claremont played along. Likewise, there's also the possibility that Claremont had already conceived the concept beforehand, and Mantlo, knowing his future intentions for the character, simply decided to implement the first hints in Roms pages. The briefly hinted romance between Rogue and Rom was never revisited. Rogue is known as "Malicia" in French, "Titania" in Latin American Spanish, "Pícara" in European Spanish, "Vampira" in Portuguese, "Шельма" in Russian (also "Руж" in X-Men: Evolution and Wolverine and the X-Men), Vadóc in Hungarian, and was known as "Parasit" in Danish and "Ruda" in Polish. The issue in which Rogue joins the X-Men was voted the 49th greatest Marvel Comic of all time. Rogue was #5 on IGN's Top Twenty-Five X-Men list, and #4 on their Top Ten X-Babes list and #3 on Marvel's list of Top 10 Toughest Females for 2009 and was given title of #1 X-Man on CBR's Top 50 X-Men of All Time for 2008. Depending on the writer, Rogue's dialogue usually has 'I' replaced with 'Ah' to emphasize her southern accent. This is not the case all the time, however. Rogue reflects the stereotype of a southern belle, a woman in the South who is beautiful, flirtatious, yet chaste. Rogue's absorption of Genis-Vell's cosmic powers during was meant to be a long-lasting consequence of House of M; however, the X-Men-related books weren't interested in following this plot point, so the power upgrade only lasted as long as House of M.

rojash.name: Rojash
rojash.first_appearance: Fantastic Four: The Prodigal Sun Vol 1 1
rojash.origin: Rojash was the leader of a band of Swamp Men who came in contact with the alien Prah'd'gul after his ship crash landed in the Savage Land. After seeing him kill a Tyrannosaurus Rex, Rojash and his people kneeled before Prah'd'gul as though he was a God. Rojash took him to a citadel that once belonged to the High Evolutionary where he promised Prah'd'gul that it housed a vessel that could take him back to his own planet but the only obstacle in the way was a force field that surrounded the entire complex. Prah'd'gul used his abilities to nullify the field causing it to shut down. All of a sudden Rojash and his party were attacked by Ka-Zar and his Golden People so Rojash suggested to Prah'd'gul that they should head to their destination while they had an opening to do so. Prah'd'gul called Rojash a coward as he would not fight with his tribe. Rojash entered the tower with one of his men and found an advanced weapon which he didn't know how to operate it. He accidentally pulled the trigger which fired off a blast in the direction of his man, vaporizing him into nothing. Rojash then returned to the battle outside where he fired the weapon in Prah'd'gul's path but Ka-Zar saved him but ended up killing two of Ka-Zar's people. He then aimed it at the Fantastic Four, but Sue put up a protective field around the team causing the beam to reflect off her shield and back towards Rojash disintegrating his entire body.

rojohn smythe.name: Rojohn Smythe
rojohn smythe.origin: Coming across the lost planet Talbos in his exploration as an architect, Rojohn Smythe discovered it had been annihilated by some mysterious catastrophe that had left a measurable amount of residual radiation. Exploring the surface, he discovered that a great battle was the cause of the planet's current condition, with bones littering the streets of a once mighty city. Studying the bones, he found that some were wolf-like and some were the bones of Skrulls, and realized that the Skrulls had intended to conquer the planet, but the native populace had been more than the invaders had expected. Next, discovering a massive temple untouched by the devastation, Smythe ran to it eager to discover its mysteries. Entering the temple, Smythe felt as if he were being watched and was suddenly confronted by the sudden lighting of the brazier in a statue's grasp. Scared, Smythe froze in place, and as fumes produced by the flames grew thicker, he found himself choking on them until he heard a voice. A being representing the spirits of the Talbosians and garbed as their protector Red Wolf appeared before him and imbued him with the power of the Red Wolf. Passing out, Smythe awoke hours later and unsure if he had dreamt the experience or not, fled the planet. At a refueling station later, Smythe was passed by a group of administrators, one of whom he could, for an unknown reason, sense was a Skrull. The proximity of the Skrull triggered his first transformation as the Talbosian spirits took control of him and forced him to kill the Skrull. Later arriving at another station, a local union leader's arrival was interrupted as Smythe again was forcibly transformed into Red Wolf, killing the union leader. Stopped by the station's guards, Smythe was placed in a jail cell. After Hercules' arrival on that same station, and his subsequent arrest for the trouble he had caused elsewhere, he was placed in a cell with Smythe. Relating his story to Hercules, Smythe was again possessed by the Red Wolf when Hercules' ally Skyppi, a Skrull, arrived to free Hercules. Leaping at the Skrull, Red Wolf was stopped by Hercules and the two brawled throughout the station, eventually breaching the hull due to Red Wolf's impetuosity. Although Hercules reacted quickly enough to avoid being sucked out into space, Red Wolf was nearly lost into space -but Hercules pulled himself and Smythe to safety. Surprised at Hercules having spared him, Red Wolf decided he was in debt with the Greek god. At his request, Red Wolf distracted the guards so that Hercules, Skyppi, and their Recorder ally could escape.

roland blaisdell.name: Roland Blaisdell
roland blaisdell.first_appearance: Mutant Misadventures of Cloak and Dagger Vol 1 10
roland blaisdell.origin: Roland Blaisdell was a former presidential advisor who was chosen to lead M-Branch, a covert government scientific division. He personally selected eight men and women from a pool of patriotic volunteers and had them subjected them to extreme mutagenic experiments involving cosmic rays, gamma radiation, and combinations of both in an attempt to artificially create superhumans. These experiments were designed to replicate the abilities of the Fantastic Four and the Hulk. The resulting group was named X-Force, with each member assigned the codename of a presumed-dead X-Man. However, the process proved highly unstable. As the recruits began suffering from severe radiation poisoning, Blaisdell turned to Dr. Ilsa Moon, a top radiation specialist at Midtown Hospital, and spent a small fortune of taxpayer money to expand her laboratory facilities there. Despite her considerable expertise, she was unable to prevent Wolverine and Longshot from succumbing to their conditions, and she had no hope of saving the remaining members of X-Force. When she relayed this information to Blaisdell, he callously dismissed any further attempts at treatment, instructing her to focus instead on collecting data on their cellular decomposition, which he intended to use to improve the success rate of future experiments. As their conditions worsened, the remaining X-Force members began violently resisting sedation, choosing to meet their end on their feet like proper soldiers rather than passively wasting away. Frustrated with their defiance, Blaisdell deemed the group more trouble than they were worth and ordered his soldiers to eliminate them on sight. In the ensuing conflict, Dazzler was seemingly killed, and Rogue was wounded. Dr. Moon, unwilling to allow further casualties, placed herself between the soldiers and the remaining X-Force members. At the same time, Cloak and Dagger, who had been visiting Father Delgado at the hospital, arrived to investigate the commotion. Their unexpected presence distracted the soldiers long enough for Colossus, Storm, and Havok to escape to the rooftop with Dr. Moon. Meanwhile, Blaisdell manipulated Rogue, who was already unstable and somewhat jealous of Colossus's leadership, convincing him that it was his patriotic duty to make the ultimate sacrifice. As Rogue was being patched up, Blaisdell led his soldiers to the rooftop, where he had Colossus, Storm, Havok, and Dr. Moon cornered by two M-Branch attack helicopters. Before he could give the order to fire, Rogue arrived, now fully convinced of his duty, and tried to persuade his former teammates to surrender and accept their fates—or face him in battle. Seeing no alternative, the surviving X-Force members lashed out with their powers. Havok, whose abilities allowed him to intensify emotions, escalated Blaisdell’s paranoia, prompting him to order his soldiers to kill everyone immediately. However, Havok’s powers also induced hallucinations among the troops, causing them to fire upon the helicopters in confusion. Amid the chaos, Cloak was able to teleport himself, Dagger, Colossus, Storm, Havok, and Dr. Moon to safety. In the aftermath, Blaisdell commended Rogue, assuring him that he had made the right choice and was a credit to the uniform. When Rogue offered to hunt down his former teammates, Blaisdell dismissed the idea, confidently stating that they would all be dead soon anyway, presumably from radiation poisoning. He then shifted his focus to selecting the next batch of volunteers, undeterred by the disastrous failure of his first experiment.

When she relayed this information to Blaisdell, he callously dismissed any further attempts at treatment, instructing her to focus instead on collecting data on their cellular decomposition, which he intended to use to improve the success rate of future experiments. As their conditions worsened, the remaining X-Force members began violently resisting sedation, choosing to meet their end on their feet like proper soldiers rather than passively wasting away. Frustrated with their defiance, Blaisdell deemed the group more trouble than they were worth and ordered his soldiers to eliminate them on sight. In the ensuing conflict, Dazzler was seemingly killed, and Rogue was wounded. Dr. Moon, unwilling to allow further casualties, placed herself between the soldiers and the remaining X-Force members. At the same time, Cloak and Dagger, who had been visiting Father Delgado at the hospital, arrived to investigate the commotion. Their unexpected presence distracted the soldiers long enough for Colossus, Storm, and Havok to escape to the rooftop with Dr. Moon. Meanwhile, Blaisdell manipulated Rogue, who was already unstable and somewhat jealous of Colossus's leadership, convincing him that it was his patriotic duty to make the ultimate sacrifice. As Rogue was being patched up, Blaisdell led his soldiers to the rooftop, where he had Colossus, Storm, Havok, and Dr. Moon cornered by two M-Branch attack helicopters. Before he could give the order to fire, Rogue arrived, now fully convinced of his duty, and tried to persuade his former teammates to surrender and accept their fates—or face him in battle. Seeing no alternative, the surviving X-Force members lashed out with their powers. Havok, whose abilities allowed him to intensify emotions, escalated Blaisdell’s paranoia, prompting him to order his soldiers to kill everyone immediately. However, Havok’s powers also induced hallucinations among the troops, causing them to fire upon the helicopters in confusion. Amid the chaos, Cloak was able to teleport himself, Dagger, Colossus, Storm, Havok, and Dr. Moon to safety. In the aftermath, Blaisdell commended Rogue, assuring him that he had made the right choice and was a credit to the uniform. When Rogue offered to hunt down his former teammates, Blaisdell dismissed the idea, confidently stating that they would all be dead soon anyway, presumably from radiation poisoning. He then shifted his focus to selecting the next batch of volunteers, undeterred by the disastrous failure of his first experiment.

roland burroughs.name: Roland Burroughs
roland burroughs.origin: Roland Burroughs underwent surgery thanks to the Roxxon Oil Company, giving him gills, claws, and a bionic tail, as well as certain other physiological changes. As a result of a mistake during the surgery to give him gills, Burroughs was rendered mute. He was also given a special costume and the alias Death Adder and joined the Serpent Squad along with Sidewinder, Anaconda, and Black Mamba. The Serpent Squad's first mission was to get the Serpent Crown, and once this mission was complete, the four of them became freelance mercenaries and criminals. The Serpent Squad were later joined by a handful of other snake-themed villains and formed the highly organized team of criminals and mercenaries known as the Serpent Society. One of the Society's first missions was to kill the rogue A.I.M. leader known as M.O.D.O.K.. Death Adder was instrumental in the assassination, his poison finishing off their target. One of the other members, Princess Python, showed cowardice and betrayed them on this mission, and after her memory was wiped, he was sent to return her to her former team, the Circus of Crime. While they were in transit, the Serpent Saucer Death Adder was flying malfunctioned and crashed into the South Bronx. Leaving Princess Python in the saucer, Death Adder went to get help. He hailed and hijacked a cab which, unfortunately for him, was driven by Scourge who promptly killed him with an explosive bullet. After his death, a simulacra was created by Grandmaster to compete in battle against the Avengers in a wager against Death. More recently, Death Adder was one of many of Scourge's victims resurrected by the criminal the Hood to serve in his gang. Some time later, he joined Crime-Master's Savage Six and was killed by Venom.

roland rayburn.name: Roland Rayburn
roland rayburn.origin: A Wall Street trader unaware of his mutant ability to persuade others to do as he wished, Roland was abducted by the Arranger and brainwashed into working for the Kingpin's organization. He persuaded the Punisher to kill the Lobo Brothers, who were a threat to the Kingpin at the time. The plan was foiled by Spider-Man, with the Lobo brothers escaping. When Spider-Man was shot by a second gunman, he was at the mercy of the Punisher. The Persuader told the Punisher to kill Spider-Man, but the Punisher threw off the Persuader's control, and shot him to death.

roland taylor.origin: Roland Taylor was pushed to trying to end his life due to his divorce, his schizophrenia among other things. However, he was saved by Captain Universe and was healed of his schizophrenia becoming the new Captain Universe. He sought out his ex-wife but she didn't believe he was better. Shortly thereafter, he was attacked by the Wraith Squad who wanted to capture the weidler of Captain Universe. After escaping, the Uni-Power tried to leave, but his warped Psyche prevented it from leaving which remade Taylor into a new Captain Universe. His fate after this is unknown.

roland treece.name: Roland Treece
roland treece.origin: Roland Treece was the CEO of Treece International and a member of the Life Foundation. Seeking to displace the homeless inhabitants of the Underground City and take over it for himself, Treece came into conflict with the supervillain-turned-vigilante Venom. Desiring to get Venom out of the way of his plans, Treece formed a PMC squad called the Jury and outfitted them with anti-symbiote powered armor; later helping Life Foundation CEO Carlton Drake capture Venom. Believing Venom to be out of the way for good, Treece dispatched a squad of Digger Suits to bulldoze the Underground City, but was thwarted by Venom.

rolf kleinberg.name: Rolf Kleinberg
rolf kleinberg.origin: Rolf Kleinberg was a famous scientist in a parallel Earth where super-heroes only existed as comic-book characters. Kleinberg postulated the existence of other realities and tried to explain the relationships between them. This got the attention of Kang the Conqueror, who had accidentally discovered Kleinberg's Earth. Kang improved Kleinberg's theories: He decided that, if he could stabilize a synchronicity of events among two realities, this would irreversibly link their destinies together, with everything in the comic-books of Kleinberg's reality happening in Earth-616. Kang kidnapped and mind-controlled Kleinberg to use him as a pawn, but some time-travelling heroes Kang was trying to manipulate eventually rescued Kleinberg and defeated Kang.

rolf reibel.name: Rolf Reibel
rolf reibel.species: Human mutated from exposure to chemical gases
rolf reibel.origin: The criminal who became known as the "Green-Faced Man" was a notorious killer who was active during the 1940s. Developing various gases to kill his victims, Reibel accidentally exposed himself to one of his most recent chemical mixes. Instead of killing him, it mutated him instead, giving him green skin and pointed fangs and made him immune to poison gases. Ultimately captured and put on trial for his crimes, the Green-Faced Man had one of his minions rig a film projector with evidence of his crime to eject poison gas in the courtroom. Unleashing the deadly gas and killing everyone inside, the Green-Faced Man attempted to flee the scene. He did not count on the fact that the Patriot would be on site, assigned to cover the story in his civilian guise of newspaper reporter Jeff Mace. The Patriot chased the Green-Faced Man to the roof of the courthouse. Their fight led them off the rooftop and onto a statue of Justice. Overpowering the Green-Faced Man, the Patriot tossed him off the statue. Reibel saved himself from a deadly fall by grabbing onto one of the hands of a clock below. However, this was only a slight reprieve as the Patriot jumped down, grabbed the opposing arm of the clock, and used it to swing around to Reibel and knock him loose again. The Green-Faced Man then fell to the pavement below, dying on impact.

rom.name: Rom
rom.origin: ===Beginnings=== 200px||thumb|right|With Karas Rom was born on the planet Galador in the midst of its most prosperous era. He was a poet. During his youth, he went swimming in a waterfall with his friend Karas, who ultimately saved him from drowning by pulling him to shore after he was swept away by the current. In their culture, saving someone's life is considered sacred, so this experience strengthened the bond between the two. The peaceful Galadorian species was renowned for traveling across the universe with the sole, benevolent purpose of sharing their wisdom and technological advancements with more primitive races. One day, despite repeated warnings, Galador's stubborn fleet ventured into a remote star system known as the Dark Nebula. There, they were ambushed by the Dire Wraiths, a hostile race of shape-shifting aliens from the Wraithworld who had no interest in charity. The fleet attempted to defend itself but was ultimately decimated by a shadowy creature known as the Deathwing, summoned by the Wraiths. With the fleet annihilated, the Wraiths turned their attention to Galador itself, beginning to plot its destruction. The news spread quickly among the civilian population, and thousands of Galadorians, including Rom, gathered outside the temple of their leader, the Prime Director, to learn what actions would be taken against the impending invasion. With no other options to defend themselves, the Prime Director made a desperate plea to the young people, asking them to voluntarily undergo a surgical procedure that would turn them into armored cyborg warriors capable of confronting the threat, at the cost of losing their humanity (body parts, etc.), with the promise that they would regain it once the crisis had passed. Fully aware of the sacrifice involved, Rom was the first to bravely step forward as a volunteer. Millions followed his example, but a few hundred, including Karas and Rom himself, met the compatibility requirements to bond with the cybernetic implants. Ray-Na, Rom's lover, disapproved of his decision, fearing not only the dangers of the mission, but also that the surgery might affect her ability to feel emotions. In response, Rom reassured her, promising that his love for her would never die, no matter what. 220px||thumb|left|Being grafted onto the Spaceknight armor Days later, Rom, along with the other approved volunteers, arrived at the Hall of Science, where each of them was grafted with a Plandanium cybernetic armor connected directly to their nervous system, and equipped with a customized weapon. Rom was granted a Neutralizer that would allow him to banish his enemies to Limbo, or kill them, if the need arose. In this way, the warriors known as Spaceknights were born—Galador’s last line of defense. Together, the Spaceknights flew to the planet’s orbit, where they confronted the newly arrived Dire Wraith Warfleet. Karas, now codenamed Firefall, was the first to break formation to attack the enemy, starting the battle. He would go missing in action shortly after. The Wraiths had the numerical advantage, but the Galadorians’ determination to defend their people forced the enemy into a precarious position, prompting them to use their secret weapon once again: the Deathwing. This escalated the battle, costing dozens of knights their lives. In an act of heroism, Rom flew toward the creature and killed it by piercing its head, forcing the remaining Wraithkind to retreat. Once he regrouped with his surviving comrades, they celebrated the victory by chanting his name in unison and collectively awarded him the title of the Greatest of the Spaceknights. Unsatisfied with the enemy’s retreat, Rom decided to pursue them on his own. Rom chased the remnants of the warfleet to the Wraithworld, where he became the target of multiple attacks, all of which he effortlessly dodged. Desperate, the Wraiths cast a spell on him, making him hallucinate endless enemies surrounding him on all sides, giving them time to evacuate the planet while Rom fought the illusions in his mind. Hours later, a small squadron of Spaceknights (Raak, the Breaker, Plor, the Pulsar, Skera, the Scanner, Tarm, the Seeker, Vola, the Trapper, and Unam, the Unseen) was sent to find their comrade and managed to track him to the now deserted Wraithworld, pulling him out of his trance. Realizing that by now the Dire Wraiths were likely scattered across the cosmos, Rom told his comrades that their duty was now to fight the Wraith threat not only on Galador but throughout the entire universe. He returned to his home planet with the squadron, and together they joined the rest of their fellow Spaceknights and the Prime Director to hold a funeral ceremony for the victims of the battle in Galador’s orbit. After the cremation ritual, Rom met with Ray-Na, who couldn’t wait for her beloved to regain his humanity. Her illusions were shattered when, learning of the Wraithkind’s dispersal, the Prime Director begged the Spaceknights to remain in thei

During his youth, he went swimming in a waterfall with his friend Karas, who ultimately saved him from drowning by pulling him to shore after he was swept away by the current. In their culture, saving someone's life is considered sacred, so this experience strengthened the bond between the two. The peaceful Galadorian species was renowned for traveling across the universe with the sole, benevolent purpose of sharing their wisdom and technological advancements with more primitive races. One day, despite repeated warnings, Galador's stubborn fleet ventured into a remote star system known as the Dark Nebula. There, they were ambushed by the Dire Wraiths, a hostile race of shape-shifting aliens from the Wraithworld who had no interest in charity. The fleet attempted to defend itself but was ultimately decimated by a shadowy creature known as the Deathwing, summoned by the Wraiths. With the fleet annihilated, the Wraiths turned their attention to Galador itself, beginning to plot its destruction. The news spread quickly among the civilian population, and thousands of Galadorians, including Rom, gathered outside the temple of their leader, the Prime Director, to learn what actions would be taken against the impending invasion. With no other options to defend themselves, the Prime Director made a desperate plea to the young people, asking them to voluntarily undergo a surgical procedure that would turn them into armored cyborg warriors capable of confronting the threat, at the cost of losing their humanity (body parts, etc.), with the promise that they would regain it once the crisis had passed. Fully aware of the sacrifice involved, Rom was the first to bravely step forward as a volunteer. fields.personality: Although cold, Rom is deeply magnanimous and empathetic with those around him. However, his nobility has made him vulnerable to deception, as seen when dangerous prisoners convinced him to free them by making him believe they were slaves. He has also shown an almost paternal affinity for children, who are often among the few humans unafraid of his presence. Due to his lack of humanity, he struggles to feel and express positive emotions such as joy or love, though it is not impossible for him. He has shown himself to be much more susceptible to negative emotions, such as jealousy, anger, and especially sadness, often experiencing deep depressive episodes precisely driven by his longing for his lost humanity. The most severe of these culminated in a suicide attempt. His bravery and selfless actions have been recognized by the people of Galador, Reed Richards, Prince Namor, Doctor Strange, and ultimately, all of Earth's heroes. ===Morality=== Rom is bound by the Spaceknight oath, a code of honor that forbids him from killing unless in self-defense. He has been willing to break this oath under certain circumstances, such as defending innocent lives, or facing higher-level threats like Hybrid, the second-generation Spaceknights, and Doctor Dredd. Although he believes that no species deserves death more than the Dire Wraiths, and the Spaceknight oath apparently allows for their execution, Rom voluntarily chose to banish them to Limbo instead. He seems to consider his "no-killing Wraiths rule" to be purely personal, as he has no problem letting beings other than himself eliminate them. He has shown mercy and empathy to those Wraiths who have proven they can change for the better, such as Jacob Marks and Michael Baran. ===Relationships=== Rom's first lover was the Galadorian Ray-Na, who inspired him to continue his duty as a Spaceknight even when he wished to return to his human form. Later, she died in his arms, a victim of the Dire Wraiths. Two hundred years later, Rom still remembered her with pain and sadness from time to time. During their time serving together, the Spaceknight Starshine fell in love with him, but her feelings were not reciprocated. After touching him in an attempt to steal his powers, the mutant Rogue ended up absorbing his nobility and kindness. Experiencing these qualities firsthand made her fall deeply in love with him, to the point of being willing to risk her life to save him from Hybrid, defying Mystique's orders in the process. Despite his personal desire to never feel emotions again, Rom's heart couldn't help but reciprocate Rogue's love, which Hybrid took advantage of to psychologically attack him. Rom's primary love interest was the human Brandy Clark. As the first native he encountered upon arriving on Earth and the only one who stopped to listen to the purpose of his mission, Rom continued turning to her to learn more about the planet, and eventually, they developed mutual feelings. However, due to his lack of humanity, Rom considered himself incapable of truly loving her as she deserved, so he chose to flee from both her and his own emotions. Brandy loved him enough to sacrifice her own humanity, becoming a Spacknight to be like him and be by his side, even in his pain, a decision Rom disapproved of. After regaining their human forms, they married, had two children, and became the rulers of Galador. Without a corpse, Brandy found it very difficult to accept Rom's presumed death, making her susceptible to manipulation by Volx and Klobok. ===Religion=== Like other Galadorians, Rom frequently shouts the expression “Gods of Galador!” On one occasion, he even prayed to them.
transportation: Rocket-pods: These are a pair of powerful thrusters located on the back of his armor that allow Rom to fly great distances.
fields.notes: ===Original Toy=== 260px|thumb|right|Original 1979 ROM: The Space Knight toy The original Rom comic book was produced to complement ROM: The Space Knight, a toy created by inventor Bryan Lawrence "Bing" McCoy and released by the company in 1979. The comic was successful enough to continue publishing even after the failure and the subsequent discontinuation of the toy it was ironically intended to advertise. In 1985, Parker Brothers merged with , forming Kenner Parker Toys, Inc. Kenner Parker Toys was acquired by in 1987, which in turn was eventually purchased by in 1991, placing the Rom character and franchise under its ownership. Since they were created exclusively for the comic, several key elements of Roms lore, such as Galador and almost all of the Spaceknights (except Rom himself), are the sole property of Marvel. The Dire Wraiths were first mentioned in a promotional video created by Parker Brothers to showcase the figure at the Toy Fair in February 1979. Therefore, they do not fall into this category. Marvel was unaware of this and, believing it owned the rights, continued using them for years even after losing the Rom license. In 2016, it filed a legal opposition against Hasbro for registering the name as a trademark for use in the ROM comic by IDW Publishing, which was released that same year. Ultimately, it was clarified that ownership of at least the name belonged to Hasbro, leading Marvel to withdraw its claim. Despite this, the publisher still retains full ownership over the original designs it created for the Wraiths, which forced IDW to extensively redesign its versions. Contrary to popular belief, Bing McCoy did not completely sell his creation to Parker Brothers. Instead, he reached a mutual agreement with the company that allowed him to retain the rights to secondary merchandising. This means that not only did McCoy receive royalties from the profits of the Rom comic, but he and his family still hold a certain degree of authority over the franchise, though the extent of this is unknown. Rom was described as a "Space Knight" (two words) on his original toy packaging (see above). On the other hand, in the comics, they opted for the spelling "Spaceknight" (one word). Unintentionally, this allowed Marvel to retain the Spaceknights trademark even without Rom's rights. Either way, Marvel later reclaimed the "Space Knight" trademark, though apparently only for strictly non-Rom-related uses, such as the title of the comic series , the episode title , the group of Peran Space Knights, and Aeon the Knife. ===License Issues=== Due to the expiration of its contract with Parker Brothers, Marvel lost the license to Rom sometime after the conclusion of his original series in 1986. The publisher retained the rights to all the original material it had created for the Rom comic, but it could no longer use the character's distinct likeness or even reprint previously published stories. This restriction also applied to issues of Marvel-owned characters that featured significant appearances by Rom. While the early and mid-1990s saw a few minor appearances and explicit mentions of the character in issues like (1994) and (1996), factors such as the , enacted in 1998, led companies like Hasbro to further reinforce protections over their intellectual properties. This further restricted Marvel's ability to use Rom, ultimately leading the publisher to kill him off-panel in (2000), a limited series sequel to Rom that continued Galador’s story with Rom’s son, Prince Tristan, as the protagonist. The comic emphasizes that Rom's body was never found, deliberately leaving the door open for a hypothetical return of the character in the future. Marvel would create new characters based on Rom and appear to be his replacement. These were Roamer, a former Spaceknight who became a mercenary before returning to his heroic duty, and Morn, the legendary "First Spaceknight" though that title belonged to Rom. The events of Rom, like those of other licensed comics of the time, were too deeply integrated into Marvel's Prime Universe to be ignored. As a result, they have remained canon within continuity and have been referenced multiple times, with characters originating from the series, such as Hybrid and the Spaceknights, appearing in other titles. However, the central character himself remained in the shadows, with nothing more than indirect mentions andindirect mentions and nondescript appearances commonly known as lawyer-friendly cameos. Two lists will be presented below: one that compiles his appearances after the loss of license—and how Marvel managed to evade copyright—and another that details the omissions made in the reprints to avoid legal problems. ====Nondescript Cameos==== 200px|thumb|right|Rom, as he is depicted in Spaceknights (April, 1994): Rom and Brandy Clark are among the guests at the wedding of Marlo Chandler and Rick Jones. He does not wear his armor, however, since at that time his legal protection was not so str
fields.trivia: ===Fictional trivia=== 280px|thumb|right|In her 4th appearance, Rogue absorbs Rom's kindness by kissing him Indirectly, Rom was responsible for Rogue becoming a hero. In , the then-villain kisses the Spaceknight in an attempt to steal his powers but accidentally absorbs his nobility and bravery instead, making her his ally for the remainder of the issue. Although the effect is temporary, experiencing these feelings—perhaps for the first time—was the turning point that set her on the path to her redemption arc, which would later be continued in . It is known that writers Bill Mantlo and Chris Claremont were frequent collaborators, but it's unclear whether Mantlo was the first to propose the idea of redeeming Rogue and then Claremont played along, or if, on the contrary, it was Claremont who had already conceived the concept beforehand, and Mantlo, knowing about it, simply decided to implement early hints in the pages of Rom. This also makes Rom the first of many love interests Rogue would have, historically speaking. Despite the implication in the final panel of that story, this plot thread remained a , and the romance between Rom and Rogue was never revisited. 200px|thumb|right As an , Rom was shown as a diegetic toy on more than once: : Toys of Rom and the Microducks (a parody of the Micronauts) can be seen in Duckworld. As expected, they are represented as anthropomorphic ducks. : Scott Lang shrank to fit inside a Rom doll to repair it for his daughter, Cassie. Interestingly, Scott met the real Rom in person during the Wraith War. : A Rom doll is among the items Doctor Octopus tries to steal from a toy store. Unlike Cassie's, this one is drawn to look more like his real-life Parker Brothers action figure. Rom's profile in the suggests that he was two hundred years old when he became a Spaceknight. Considering it took him another two hundred years to reach Earth from Galador, it can be estimated that Rom was approximately four hundred years old when the events of his original comic series began. However, since the chronology of (which takes place at least two decades after Rom, according to a comment by Balin in issue #3) conflicts with the Sliding Timescale of Earth-616 (which spans only fifteen years), it can be assumed that time on Galador moves faster than on Earth. This implies that Rom could be significantly younger than thought if his age is measured in human years, and would explain the premature aging that Brandy Clark shows in , a story that aligns better with Timescale despite occurring after Spaceknights. Rom and Ikon are the only Spaceknights who do not appear to possess any codenames, as they are always referred to by their real names. Possibly this is a common treatment given to those who hold the position of Greatest of the Spaceknights. Rom means "Before All Others" in Galadorian language. Rom used to be a poet before becoming a Spaceknight. He dedicated odes to peace. Rick Jones used to own a costume, a helmet, and an unfinished statue of Rom. In , when Conan mentions Crom, Venom becomes confused and asks if he means the Spaceknight, a clear reference to Rom. In , a robot waiter with a head reminiscent of Rom's can be seen. On his abdomen is a bottle labeled "RUM SPACE KNIGHT," confirming that it is indeed an intentional reference. ===Real-world trivia=== As its owner, Hasbro has released a variety of non-Marvel-related products based on the ROM franchise. They planned to release a figure of Rom (reimagined as a character) in the Bot Shots toyline. A copy was presented at the 2013 Toy Fair, but the figure never went on sale. A Rom toy (not under the Marvel brand) was released as an exclusive at 2014. In December 2015, Hasbro Studios, LLC (now known as ) announced it was working in collaboration with to produce a ROM movie, set in a derived from the first live-action . Two years later, it was announced that Zak Penn had signed on as a screenwriter. However, the project ultimately ended up in , cancelled. Co-written by Chris Ryall and Christos N. Gage, a new ROM comic series published by IDW Publishing arrived in 2016. This one was set within , which allowed the character to interact with other toy franchises that also once had a Marvel-licensed title, such as G.I. Joe, Inhumanoids, Visionaries, Transformers, and the Micronauts—the latter also by Bill Mantlo. In addition to his main series, Rom starred in three other limited series until 2020 (Rom vs. Transformers: Shining Armor, Rom & the Micronauts, and Rom: Dire Wraiths), and had involvement during the Revolution, Reconstruiction, Revolutionaries, and Unicron events. Thanks to the crossover, IDW's Hasbro Comic Book Universe is—more or less—canon within the Marvel multiverse (being theoretically set on Earth-7642), so one could argue that technically its version of Rom is as well, but since he never actually crossed paths with any of the Marvel properties, he doesn't qualify for an article on this wiki. roma.origin: thumb|left|Roma in ===Origins=== Roma is the daughter of Merlyn and, like him, exists as a gestalt of her counterparts throughout the Multiverse. Although more than four billion years old by the standards of her people, she was still considered comparatively young. She spent eons assisting Merlyn in the protection of the Omniverse, but differed from her father by placing greater value on compassion and the lives affected by their plans. ===Captain Britain=== Anticipating threats that would eventually arise from Mad Jim Jaspers and Necrom, Merlyn sent James Braddock to Earth-616 to establish a line of potential champions. Years later, when James' son Brian Braddock was nearly killed by the Reaver, Roma appeared alongside Merlyn as the Lady of the Northern Skies. They offered Brian a choice between the Sword of Might and the Amulet of Right; his rejection of violence led him to choose the Amulet and become Captain Britain. Roma subsequently observed Brian's early development while remaining disguised and allowing him to believe that she and Merlyn were merely figures from legend. On another world, Roma and Merlyn offered the same choice to Bran Bardic, a soldier hardened by an unending war. When he chose the Sword of Might, Roma judged him unsuitable and attempted to revoke his power, but Merlyn overruled her out of curiosity and allowed Bardic to become Albion. After Lord Hawk left Brian comatose, Roma drew his spirit into Otherworld. She helped him confront his fear and self-doubt before equipping him with the Star Sceptre, which allowed him to fly and return to his body. When Otherworld was invaded by the Nethergods commanded by Necromon, Roma helped Merlyn reinforce Camelot's defenses while Captain Britain and the Black Knight searched for the missing King Arthur. Roma personally led Camelot's knights against the trolls and goblins besieging the castle until Arthur returned and defeated Necromon. ===Jaspers' Warp and Omniversal Guardian=== Merlyn later sent Brian and Jackdaw to the devastated Earth-238, where the reality's Jaspers had ordered the extermination of superhumans. After the Fury killed both heroes, Roma and Merlyn recovered Brian's remains and resurrected him: Merlyn reconstructed his mind while Roma rebuilt and strengthened his body, making the powers formerly generated by his costume an innate part of him. Roma was unaware that Merlyn had expected Brian to die and intended his resurrection to draw the Fury to Earth-616, where it could be used against that world's more dangerous Jaspers. The Fury followed Brian to Earth-616 and ultimately destroyed Jaspers after their reality-warping conflict. Merlyn then staged his own death to lure Necrom out of hiding, but kept Roma ignorant of the deception. Believing her father had truly been killed, she summoned the Captain Britain Corps to Otherworld and presided over his state funeral alongside Captain Britain, Captain U.K., the Black Knight, King Arthur, and Saturnyne. Roma succeeded Merlyn as Omniversal Guardian and assumed responsibility for the Corps, although Saturnyne retained considerable administrative authority as Omniversal Majestrix. Roma later sent Captain U.K. to liberate Earth-794 from Sat-Yr-9 and restored Linda's murdered husband, Rick, to life as an act of restitution. She also brought members of the Corps to Otherworld so that they could train together and become aware of one another, while quietly placing Saturnyne under closer observation. ===The Adversary and the X-Men=== Continuing another of Merlyn's long-term plans, Roma worked with the Cheyenne shaman Naze to prepare Forge for a confrontation with the Adversary. Because Forge had rejected the mystical heritage needed to defeat the entity, Roma and Naze maneuvered events that would force him to reconcile it with his technological abilities. Disguised as an ordinary woman, Roma encouraged Colossus to rejoin the X-Men before allowing the Adversary to capture her. Forge eventually used the willing life forces of the X-Men to seal the Adversary away, apparently killing the entire team as the event was broadcast around the world. Roma restored the X-Men to life almost immediately, but allowed the public to continue believing that they were dead and made them undetectable by conventional electronic equipment. Before sending them to Australia, she entrusted the team with the Siege Perilous, a mystical portal capable of judging those who passed through it and granting them new lives. ===Formation of Excalibur=== Roma then completed Merlyn's plan to unite five heroes against Necrom. She used dreams and visions to alert Nightcrawler, Shadowcat, and Meggan that Rachel Summers was being held by Mojo, then sent the Technet to recover Rachel in a deliberately heavy-handed operation. The resulting struggle brought the four together with Captain Britain and led to the formation of Excalibur. Although more than four billion years old by the standards of her people, she was still considered comparatively young. roman.name: Roman
roman.origin: Roman was a rival of the Pazzo Family. In public he dressed as an ancient Roman, acting as if he was insane so that law enforcement wouldn't arrest him and if brought to trail he wouldn't be convicted. In private the crimelord was well-mannered and sophisticated. He lived in a mansion with an interior built to resemble a Roman villa, with columns and statues. Roman had a trap door that led to a room full of lions, to whom he fed his enemies and those who broke his rules. He attempted to feed Wolverine to the lions, but was fed to them by Wolverine.

roman nekoboh.name: Roman Nekoboh
roman nekoboh.origin: Roman Nekoboh is a famed musician, actor and a world renowned celebrity. Despite his old age he has maintained a public persona as a vigorous and attractive man. Nekoboh was scheduled to meet Alison Blaire in a publicity event organized by Nick Brown when he got a visit from his accountant about his dire financial situation. As a remedy, he decided to produce a new movie co-starring Alison as damsel in distress. After meeting her at the event he took her on a vanity flight on his private plane where he made romantic approaches towards her with the excuse of discussing the movie's "love scenes". His approach was interrupted by an unmarked fighter jet shooting down his airplane. After getting rescued from the falling plane (alongside his pilot Hack) by a quick thinking Alison, he made a quick recovery. He kept in touch with Alison and acted as her agent, inviting her to the Hollywood party at which she met Bob Benson. Although he tried to warn her about Bob, Alison got involved in the director's schemes and ended up exposing them. Still chasing the possibility of a relationship with her, Nekoboh made increasingly brazen moves towards Alison. In one instance he followed her with his car, stole her mail and entered her apartment after her, but Alison made him give her mail back and leave her apartment. He later announced her co-stardom in his movie without asking her, leading to the paparazzi asking her questions about their supposed romantic relationship. Meanwhile Roman gained access to her apartment through her super (who was a fan of his) and upon Alison's arrival forced himself onto her. Upon Alison's insistence that he leave her apartment, he threatened her with the end of her career and left. However he returned the following morning to chase Alison in his car. After driving backwards and making an illegal u-turn, Alison blew out his tires using a laser. Undeterred, Roman kept chasing her on foot and faked a heart attack to get her to check on him. Noting that she was reading the employment opportunities section of the newspaper, he managed to convince her to listen to his proposal over a cup of coffee. Nekoboh took Alison to a luxurious restaurant and revealed his financial situation to her, offering a role in his movie with "no strings attached". He went on to purchase her luxury clothing and a new house, and took her to high society events to "get seen". Alison gradually softened her attitude against him and their relationship quickly turned into a romance. The movie in question could only get the backing of Eric Beale due to Alison's past association with the X-men. Having been rejected by Alison himself, Beale had ulterior motives. He ordered Roman to find out if Alison was a mutant, and after her reveal to him that she was, he made him leak the information to the press under the guise of a publicity stunt. He managed to convince Alison that if they managed to make their movie they could save the reputation of mutants once and for all. As the topic of the movie changed from swashbuckling pirates to mutant struggle, Alison's role in the movie changed from a damsel in distress to a super heroine and their roles in the relationship also switched. After his co-star's reveal as a mutant, the existing anti-mutant hysteria turned into riots against Nekoboh. A mob attacked the couple on a private screening and Alison had to use her powers against the mob to save them. Later, he was summoned to Beale Productions and forced to sign a strict employment contract prohibiting him from seeing Alison again. He attempted to return and tear the contract, but he was stopped by Alison who had already burned it alongside the what they thought was the last print of their movie. Alison soon left Roman, declaring she wanted to make it on her own. Roman managed to pay his debts using the front payment for the movie.

romantic objective pamela.name: Romantic Objective Pamela
romantic objective pamela.origin: Romantic Objective Pamela was a member of the Masters of the Mental Arts, defenders of the planet Yann. When volcanic upheavals imperiled Yannians, their leader ,and Pamela's romantic interest, Christopher Ganyrog lead the Masters on a rescue mission, only to encounter the Defenders who had been transported to Yann. The two teams realized their common enemy in Yandroth and the threat he represented to both their planets. Bringing the full might of the Masters, the team transported to Earth to "run interference" between the heroes of Earth (whose actions might unwittingly cause the destruction of the planet) and Yandroth's schemes. The plan succeeded and Yandroth was taken back to Yann for trial. Yandroth later escaped custody and killed Pamela and Ganyrog.

romany wisdom.name: Romany Wisdom
romany wisdom.origin: The estranged elder sister of Pete Wisdom, Romany met and fell in love with Joseph Chapman, the third man to wear the Union Jack super-hero mantle. Eventually, they broke up under unclear circumstances, but apparently remained somewhat of friends afterward. She even occasionally helped Jack during his super-hero adventures. She grew interested in history, and came to know a lot about ancient cultures such as vampires. Once, Pete was forced to make contact with his estranged family, visiting his borderline-senile father (to get a professional profiling on the killer) and his sister (who could translate the symbols found on the bodies). With Romany's help, they determined that the murderer delusionally believed himself to be Cain, son of Adam, and was composing a letter directly to God on the corpses he was leaving behind, asking for forgiveness and to be allowed admittance into heaven. Much later, Romany apparently perished in an explosion, but her brother was suspicious she was actually still alive.

romeo inhuman.origin: ===Origins=== Romeo is an Inhuman with empathic abilities. He dropped out of high school after a disastrous attempt to show affection to his crush, a fellow member of the wrestling team. Following three months of flirting with him, Romeo stole a kiss from the boy, and got punched in the face in return. Romeo also enjoyed running and gaming. ===Working for the Inhuman Royal Family=== After gaining superpowers when his latent Inhuman genes were activated by the Terrigen Bomb's wandering cloud, Romeo began working with the Royal Inhuman Diplomatic Mission, in order to use his powers to calm down those Inhumans who had just emerged confused from their Terrigenesis cocoons. One of the Inhumans he assisted was Doris Bray, in the Sonoran Desert of Arizona. During another mission in Miami, Romeo crossed paths with the X-Man Iceman. After the Inhuman they were looking for was subdued, Romeo left with the other members of the Diplomatic Mission, but not before leaving his phone number in Iceman's phone. The following weeks, Romeo and Bobby began dating. The first time they hung out, they went jogging on a mountain. The second date they went laser-tagging. On the third date, they hung out with some of the young X-Men and an Inhuman named Sasha. thumb|left|Romeo and Bobby Drake On the day of their fourth date, the different mutant factions decided to assault New Attilan in order to neutralize major Inhuman players so they could destroy the Terrigen Cloud with no interference, because it was about to disperse into Earth's atmosphere, making the planet uninhabitable for mutants. Iceman decided to take part on the attack solely so he could slip away from the rest of the mutants once they entered New Attilan and find Romeo. Once Bobby found Romeo in one of the rooms in the zone under lockdown for non-combatant Inhumans, they shared their first kiss and escaped together. Romeo and Bobby's relationship was short-lived, however, and Romeo eventually stopped seeing Bobby. ===Fall of X=== During a dimension jumping event with the Royal Inhuman Diplomatic Mission, Romeo was stranded in another dimension for a decade. Once he finally returned to Earth, virtually no time had passed. He resumed his relationship with Bobby, who also was an adult, after having returned to the past, and started helping him fight criminals like Anuxa. thumb|right|Romeo at the Ice Palace. Romeo participated at the third Hellfire Gala with his boyfriend. When Nimrod crashed the party and killed most of the newly elected X-Men members, Iceman attacked the Sentinel directly. Unfortunately he was defeated and melt down in front of Romeo, who managed to save himself, by teleporting to New York City via Lourdes Chantel's powers. After the Gala, he went to Antarctica and used his powers to gather all of Bobby's molecules dispersed in space and reconstruct his body. Since Bobby was still very weak and incapable of maintaining his body while leaving Antarctica, Romeo stayed in the newly built Ice Palace's War Room. Romeo's job was to inform Bobby about people in need around the world.

Romeo also enjoyed running and gaming. ===Working for the Inhuman Royal Family=== After gaining superpowers when his latent Inhuman genes were activated by the Terrigen Bomb's wandering cloud, Romeo began working with the Royal Inhuman Diplomatic Mission, in order to use his powers to calm down those Inhumans who had just emerged confused from their Terrigenesis cocoons. One of the Inhumans he assisted was Doris Bray, in the Sonoran Desert of Arizona. During another mission in Miami, Romeo crossed paths with the X-Man Iceman. After the Inhuman they were looking for was subdued, Romeo left with the other members of the Diplomatic Mission, but not before leaving his phone number in Iceman's phone. The following weeks, Romeo and Bobby began dating. The first time they hung out, they went jogging on a mountain. The second date they went laser-tagging. On the third date, they hung out with some of the young X-Men and an Inhuman named Sasha. thumb|left|Romeo and Bobby Drake On the day of their fourth date, the different mutant factions decided to assault New Attilan in order to neutralize major Inhuman players so they could destroy the Terrigen Cloud with no interference, because it was about to disperse into Earth's atmosphere, making the planet uninhabitable for mutants. Iceman decided to take part on the attack solely so he could slip away from the rest of the mutants once they entered New Attilan and find Romeo. Once Bobby found Romeo in one of the rooms in the zone under lockdown for non-combatant Inhumans, they shared their first kiss and escaped together. Romeo and Bobby's relationship was short-lived, however, and Romeo eventually stopped seeing Bobby. ===Fall of X=== During a dimension jumping event with the Royal Inhuman Diplomatic Mission, Romeo was stranded in another dimension for a decade. Once he finally returned to Earth, virtually no time had passed. He resumed his relationship with Bobby, who also was an adult, after having returned to the past, and started helping him fight criminals like Anuxa. thumb|right|Romeo at the Ice Palace. Romeo participated at the third Hellfire Gala with his boyfriend. When Nimrod crashed the party and killed most of the newly elected X-Men members, Iceman attacked the Sentinel directly. Unfortunately he was defeated and melt down in front of Romeo, who managed to save himself, by teleporting to New York City via Lourdes Chantel's powers. After the Gala, he went to Antarctica and used his powers to gather all of Bobby's molecules dispersed in space and reconstruct his body. Since Bobby was still very weak and incapable of maintaining his body while leaving Antarctica, Romeo stayed in the newly built Ice Palace's War Room. Romeo's job was to inform Bobby about people in need around the world.

romesh dalton.name: Romesh Dalton
romesh dalton.origin: Romesh Dalton was an operative for Alpha Flight. When Captain Marvel established Gamma Flight to find the Hulk, Romesh gave Walter Langkowski a report on their difficulty to track him down. He would later report when Alpha Flight's satellites got a hit on the Hulk's gamma signature in the Los Diablos Missile Base. After Shadow Base leader General Fortean raided the Alpha Flight Low-Orbit Space Station to retrieve the Gamma-Activated Tissue secured by Gamma Flight, Romesh tracked down his translocation signal back to its source in Shadow Base Site B. When Roxxon launched an attack on Phoenix, Arizona to draw out the Hulk, Romesh alerted Gamma Flight when Alpha Flight's sytems detected both the familiar energy signatures for the Hulk and his allies as well as new signatures from Roxxon's monsters. Dalton would later be doing maintenance at Alpha Flight's suspended animation lounge when Doc Samson returned to life in Langkowski's body, which was being stored in cold.

rommbu.name: Rommbu
rommbu.origin: Rommbu first arrived on Earth when his race sent him to the planet in order to demand humanity's surrender before they conquered the planet. When the humans refused, he went to his spaceship, but unknown to him, John Hunter had snuck aboard, trying to escape from the police. Rommbu eventually found John and demanded that he show Rommbu a safe place to land and recharge his ship, so John led him to the inside of an active volcano before an eruption, killing himself and seemingly killing Rommbu. Rommbu, however, survived and was one of the monsters captured by the Collector and placed in his zoo of giant monsters hidden deep beneath Canada. During an assault by the Mole Man the Collector's security systems failed, allowing all of the creatures to escape. They eventually made their way to New York City through the Mole Man's tunnels and proceeded to go on a rampage, terrorizing the city. The monsters were opposed by the Thing, the Hulk, the Beast and Giant-Man. After they had dispatched all of the monsters, they transported them all through a portal into the Negative Zone, where they would be unable to harm the people of Earth. Years later, Rommbu would escape the Negative Zone some time later and managed to reach Monster Isle. The inhabitants would be attacked by the Hunter of Monster Special Force, the alien himself would lose his left arm as he fled. Rommbu eventually returned with his arm fully regenerated, since Giant-Man claimed to be fighting him in a San Francisco park. During the Leviathons' invasion, Rommbu was among the monsters that appeared in San Diego. Rommbu assisted in the fight against the Leviathons. Kei Kawade later teleported Rommbu to Texas in order to help the Guardians of the Galaxy.

romulus.name: Romulus
romulus.species: Mutant, falsely claimed to be a “Lupine”
romulus.origin: thumb|left|Romulus in Ancient Rome ===Origin=== Romulus claimed to hail from the depths of prehistory, asserting his lineage as one of the Lupine, an ancient tribe of feral humans whose origins diverged from conventional evolutionary theories. Black Panther speculated that these primal beings might have descended from canines rather than primates, adding an intriguing layer to Romulus's enigmatic past. Leading an army of the Lupine, he embarked on a relentless campaign of conquest, subjugating numerous neighboring human tribes with ruthless efficiency. His reign of terror was marked by unparalleled brutality, exemplified by his unforgiving treatment of his own warriors. Any sign of failure was met with swift and merciless retribution, as he spared no expense in enforcing absolute loyalty and obedience among his ranks. Yet, beneath this facade of Lupine ancestry lay a labyrinth of deceit. Remus, his twin sister, eventually confessed to Wolverine that the tale of their canine origins was a lie. It was a carefully crafted subterfuge, ingeniously woven to divert attention while Romulus pursued a far more sinister agenda: the harvesting of Adamantium. The discovery of bones in the elephant graveyard served as yet another facet of this elaborate ruse, designed to ensnare Wolverine in a web of distraction. While he grappled with the mysteries presented before him, Romulus operated in the shadows, advancing his schemes unchecked. ===Across the Ages=== For centuries, Romulus and his twin sister, Remus, wielded their influence behind the scenes, their plans shaping the ebb and flow of civilizations. From the heights of the Greek Empire to the founding of Rome itself, they stood as silent architects, their actions inspiring the legends of the twin founders, . In the annals of history, Romulus's reign over Rome during the heights of the Roman Empire remains a shadowy enigma. Tales speak of his imperial rule, his dominion marked by grandeur and spectacle. Among his infamous exploits, Romulus orchestrated extravagant gladiatorial contests, pitting his Lupine warriors against ferocious beasts in the blood-soaked sands of the Colosseum. One such spectacle, etched in the annals of infamy, saw rival factions of Lupines, distinguished by their blonde hair and black hair, clash amidst the roars of tigers. As the dust settled and the beasts lay defeated, Romulus, arbiter of fate, delivered his verdict with a chilling thumbs-down gesture. The ensuing carnage, a brutal testament to his inscrutable will, saw one Lupine faction annihilate the other, their loyalty unwavering to their enigmatic master. Yet, as shadows of doubt crept over Romulus's legacy, revelations emerged from the lips of Remus herself. The Lupines, the very instruments of Romulus's power, were but figments of his elaborate myth. Across the ages, Romulus's influence endured, weaving its tendrils through the tumultuous currents of history. Working with the ravaging hordes of the Huns, who laid waste to Rome's grandeur, his unseen hand guided the course of nations, forever enigmatic, forever shrouded in mystery. ===Meeting Wolverine=== In the 1910s Romulus encountered the feral mutant Wolverine for the first time in Madripoor. He was working for the Ninja cult called the Hand and hired the freelancer on a mission to Tokyo where he encountered Sabretooth. ===World War II=== During World War II he collaborated with the Third Reich using their dark power and influence for his own ends. He used Sabretooth as an operative during the war. He assigned Sabretooth alongside a Nazi battalion, they were sent to the Italian Alps to confront Wolverine and Captain America in a fierce battle. It was during this confrontation that Logan faced off against Sabretooth. In a desperate move, Sabretooth hurled a grenade, causing Wolverine to plummet over a cliff and crash to the ground below, all while Romulus observed from the shadows. ===Raising Daken=== In post-War Japan Romulus kept an eye on Wolverine and his new bride Itsu. However, a temporal incident occurred at this time when Itsu was possessed by Omega Red. Wolverine's mind travelled back to his old body to save his possessed wife. Romulus was shocked by the confusing incident and intervened to stop the time travelling fiend from killing Wolverine. Wolverine protected Itsu and Romulus escaped into the shadows once again with the timeline restored. In 1946, Japan, Romulus hired the Winter Soldier to kill Wolverine's wife Itsu who was in the last stages of her pregnancy. After Itsu's death, Romulus took the baby Daken, cutting him from his mother's womb and leaving her body behind. The baby survived the incident, possibly due to his mutant healing factor, which he inherited from his father. When Daken's powers developed he killed his adopted parents in rage. He was found by Romulus to raise the boy to be a ruthless killer. He taught the boy that he was different and that the humans would fear him. He revealed that he could hide i

fields.trivia: Like his sister Remus, Romulus shares his name with one of the of Rome's foundation myth. In the myth they were also stated to be the sons of Aeneas, the son of Venus. It was originally intended for Wolverine's Adamantium claws to be part of his gloves rather than part of his body. But this idea was rejected by Chris Claremont. This concept was used for Romulus' Adamantium claws. According to Chris Claremont, Apocalypse was originally intended to be the true mastermind behind the Weapon X Program.

romulus augustulus.name: Romulus Augustulus
romulus augustulus.origin: ===Early Life=== Born in AD 463, Romulus' original surname was Augustus, but it was changed to the diminutive when he took the throne in AD 475 while still a child of 12. The child Emperor was described as a puppet ruler who was not recognized as a legitimate ruler; he ruled for only about one year until AD 476, when his father was defeated by the German Goth , marking the beginning of the in Europe. Thus the Empire ended with his rule, and Italy was fractured into smaller kingdoms. Romulus was not killed, however, but rather banished from the kingdom, swearing to return one day. 300px|thumb|left ===6th century=== Taking the name "Tyrannus", Augustus became a servant of the Olympian god Pluto, who empowered the former Emperor and sent him to destroy Merlin. He was sent to Britannia to conquer the kingdom of Camelot and take the throne from King Arthur. He was stopped by Merlin's champion, the Black Knight; Sir Percy of Scandia. He was no match against the young knight and fled, leaving his master, Pluto, to continue the battle, who ultimately lost and retreated back to his realm. Merlin found Romulus and banished him beneath the Earth to the underground realm known as Subterranea. ===Subterranea=== Trapped beneath the Earth; Romulus came upon an abandoned stockpile of Deviant technology, which he used to attack the surface world. On one such attack he discovered the Fountain of Youth, which allowed him to remain young throughout the long centuries. ===19th century=== In 1862, Tyrannus led an invasion force of his Tyrannoids from Subterranea, bursting through the ground and interrupting a battle during the American Civil War. ===The Modern Age=== He later attempted to conquer America by kidnapping Betty Ross and holding her hostage, thus preventing her father from resisting him. The Hulk and Rick Jones followed but they, too, were captured by Tyrannus and he used Betty as a tool against them. They eventually freed her and the trio escaped Tyrannus and trapped him underground. The Mole Man, Tyrannus' one major rival in regards to the rule of Subterranea, stole the "Fountain of Youth," causing him to age rapidly. He teleported the Hulk to Subterranea in hopes of recapturing the fountain. He was successful and was able to restore his youth and returned the Hulk to the surface world. He kidnapped and forced scientist Dr. Ralph Roberts to design a robot called the Cobalt-Robot, a giant machine used in his conflict against the Mole Man, but the mutant super-hero team the X-Men came to his rescue and stopped his plans dead in their tracks. Still angry at his past defeats against the Hulk, he sought revenge by using Deviant technology to drive the creature insane and send him on a destructive rampage. He brought him beneath the surface and sent him against the Mole Man along with Mogul, one of his other robot slaves. On another occasion, Tyrannus became lovers with Kala the Queen of the Netherworlders, another race that also lived in Subterranea. ===Nova=== Tyrannus returned to the surface world once again using Earth-Shaker, a giant humanoid boring robot. He was confronted by Nova, who battled Tyrannus and his Tyrannoids and destroyed Earth-Shaker. He then captured Tyrannus and, in defeat, he agreed to leave peacefully, retreating beneath the surface of the Earth. ===They Who Wield Power=== Having failed several times to conquer the surface world through means of force and technology, Romulus decided to try another approach. His eternal youth was failing him, so it was then that he infiltrated They Who Wield Power, the rulers of the city of El Dorado, under the identity of Des. The city's Sacred Flame of Life was a potential power source of immense energy. "They" engineered a number of crises on the surface world involving various super-heroes and super-villains that fed additional power into the Flame until it was ready to be used. At that point, Tyrannus shed his disguise and merged with the Flame himself, restoring his youth and granting him incredible powers. The child Emperor was described as a puppet ruler who was not recognized as a legitimate ruler; he ruled for only about one year until AD 476, when his father was defeated by the German Goth , marking the beginning of the in Europe. Thus the Empire ended with his rule, and Italy was fractured into smaller kingdoms. Romulus was not killed, however, but rather banished from the kingdom, swearing to return one day. 300px|thumb|left ===6th century=== Taking the name "Tyrannus", Augustus became a servant of the Olympian god Pluto, who empowered the former Emperor and sent him to destroy Merlin. He was sent to Britannia to conquer the kingdom of Camelot and take the throne from King Arthur. He was stopped by Merlin's champion, the Black Knight; Sir Percy of Scandia. He was no match against the young knight and fled, leaving his master, Pluto, to continue the battle, who ultimately lost and retreated back to his realm. Merlin found Romulus and banished him beneath the Earth to the underground realm known as Subterranea. ===Subterranea=== Trapped beneath the Earth; Romulus came upon an abandoned stockpile of Deviant technology, which he used to attack the surface world. On one such attack he discovered the Fountain of Youth, which allowed him to remain young throughout the long centuries. ===19th century=== In 1862, Tyrannus led an invasion force of his Tyrannoids from Subterranea, bursting through the ground and interrupting a battle during the American Civil War. ===The Modern Age=== He later attempted to conquer America by kidnapping Betty Ross and holding her hostage, thus preventing her father from resisting him. Still angry at his past defeats against the Hulk, he sought revenge by using Deviant technology to drive the creature insane and send him on a destructive rampage. He brought him beneath the surface and sent him against the Mole Man along with Mogul, one of his other robot slaves. On another occasion, Tyrannus became lovers with Kala the Queen of the Netherworlders, another race that also lived in Subterranea. ===Nova=== Tyrannus returned to the surface world once again using Earth-Shaker, a giant humanoid boring robot. He was confronted by Nova, who battled Tyrannus and his Tyrannoids and destroyed Earth-Shaker. fields.notes: The character of Tyrannus is based on the real life historical figure , the last Emperor of the Roman Empire before its fall. Romulus was appointed Emperor by his father Orestes on October 31, 475, and he was deposed on September 4, 476. He served as little more than a figurehead. The nickname "Augustulus" means "little Augustus" (little Emperor) and was a derisive reference to his young age. Romulus's immediate family were from the Roman province of Pannonia (covering the current areas of western Hungary, western Slovakia, eastern Austria, northern Croatia, northwestern Serbia, northern Slovenia, and northern Bosnia and Herzegovina), and many of his known family members had military backgrounds. It is not known in history when the historical Romulus died. Odoacer spared the life of the young Romulus on account of his "youth and beauty". Romulus was granted an annual pension of 6,000 solidi (the normal income of a wealthy Roman Senator) and granted an estate in Campania, near Naples, named the Castellum Lucullanum (renamed the Castel dell'Ovo). Documents of Theodoric the Great dated to 507 or 511 mention Romulus as still alive and receiving a new grant of property by a subordinate in Theodoric's court. Records about the beginning of the Gothic War (AD 535–554) in Italy do not mention Romulus at all, so modern historians presume that he had died by the early 530s. ==Clone== A Tyrannoid was given both the appearance and the memories of Tyrannus while he was involved with "They Who Wield Power." The clone was later murdered by the other Tyrannoids when they discovered just what he really was after he reverted back into a Tyrannoid.

ron rainey.origin: A talented TV actor prone to use disguises and known as "the man with the 999 faces", Ron Rainey retired from the scene and decided to start a career as a criminal impersonating Daredevil so that the hero would take the blame. In an act of mercy, Daredevil allowed Rainey to eat one Hostess Cherry Fruit Pie before sending him to jail.

ronald mutant.name: Ronald (Mutant)
ronald mutant.species: Depowered mutant, later turned into a Cyborg by Sugar Man
ronald mutant.origin: Ronny grew up with a passion for music, singing in his school choir and a band. At age thirteen, he discovered that he was a mutant able to hit notes high enough to cause powerful sonic booms. He would lose these powers on M-Day, however, and was willing to try anything to get them back. He fell in with the New Mutates, a group of young people who had been granted superhuman abilities via cybernetic implants from their mysterious benefactor, the Sugar Man. Sugar Man agreed to do the same for Ronny, on the condition that Ronny help him return home. Sugar Man outfitted Ronny with a cyborg throat apparatus. On the way to Sugar Man's portal, he met a captive of Sugar Man's, who urged Ronny to see that he was being tricked, but Ronny, blinded by his new powers, paid him no mind and stepped through the portal. Unfortunately, the dimension on the other side was not Sugar Man's home, and Ronny was almost immediately devoured by a massive predator native to the reality.
